   window's view in the library (`app/table.rs`), so every claim the window makes has a test. Nothing here enters a hash (D-012).
2. **The hero's hand is named, with its odds.** `poker::strength` names the best five cards by the engine's own category and
   enumerates every card still to come -- 19 600 flops, 1 081 turn-and-river pairs, 46 rivers -- for the chance of each better
   category; the window shows the likeliest first. Computed once per street, in the fold, never in the paint loop.
3. **Chips move, and the clock is a colour.** A street's bets fly into the pot and the pot to the winner (`gui::table::motion`, a
   model watched against successive snapshots); the seat to act wears the time it has left as its plate's colour, green to amber
   to red over the table's `action_timeout_ms` (`TableParams.action_ms`), with the ring of dots. The window repaints on its own
   while either runs and at no other time.
4. **The seats' chat is a closed group.** `TABLE_CHAT = 0x0107` (`PROTOCOL.md` section 7.8): unchained, signed by the sender's
   application key, accepted only from a key that holds a seat in the receiver's roster for the table the line names, carried on
   the table's own Tox group -- the invited set -- and on the table's GossipSub topic only where the table has no group. One line
   per two seconds per seat; a name is decoration and the seat is what the line is filed under. Muting a seat is the receiver's
   own affair and never on the wire.
5. **What else the owner asked for on the night:** the bar as PokerTH has it (chat left, the presets and the slider above Fold,
   Call, Raise and a half-height All-in, the hand's strength right), every fixed width asserted to fit the smallest window; a
   link indicator per seat from the node's own pings and closed connections (`NodeEvent::SeatLink`); a window that says the
   client is connecting to a table, with a clock, and fails after `JOIN_WAIT_MS` = 90 000 ms or on the founder's word, with *try
   again*; nothing of a hand outliving its table; the raise starting every turn at the minimum; the felt a two-to-one oval; the
   chips and their figure at twice the size.
6. **What this does not do:** the chat is not stored, not replayed and not evidence; the link figure is the libp2p ping's and
   says nothing about the Tox group; the odds are the hero's own cards against an unknown board and not an equity against
   anybody's hand.

**Guard.** `app::table` (nine tests), `app` (four), `poker::strength` (seven), `gui::table::motion` (four), `gui::table` (six),
`gui::table::paint` (three), `net::tabletalk` (seven), `protocol::messages` (the catalogue at 42), and the photographed runs named
in the `S1-CS` row.

## D-031 — heads-up, the client asks the one question D-007 leaves, and a returning opponent is dealt in again

**Built 2026-09-11 at the project owner's instruction**, from the owner's findings of the night before at the window: a heads-up
table with an absent opponent froze and said nothing, and a restarted client was not asked about its unfinished game.

1. **No certificate at two seats, still.** D-007 stands: nobody can fold a hand for an absent player heads-up, and nothing here gives
   either seat a new power. What the client adds is the question D-007's remedy implies. Once the opponent has been unreachable for
   `OPPONENT_GONE_MS` = 15 000 -- the connection closed, or no ping for `LINK_STALE_MS`; the group's count says nothing either way -- the table window asks *wait for them, or end the
   game and leave the table*, once per episode -- and, since D-046, again every thirty seconds while the player waits; a headless client writes the same sentence. A reading that reaches the opponent again
   ends the episode, and a new one asks anew. At three seats or more nothing is asked: D-023's certificate does the work.
2. **The unfinished game is asked about wherever the player is looking**, the lobby window and the table window both, and only about
   a game that can still be there: a record older than `RESUME_RECORD_MAX_AGE_MS` = 1 800 000 is dropped at start. While the client is
   trying to rejoin, D-029's give-up rule still applies.
3. **A returning opponent is dealt in again, heads-up.** `Opening::adopt` needs a strict majority of the occupied seats *other than
   the adopter's* -- the adopter signed nothing, so it is not a seat that could have agreed; heads-up that is the one other seat. A
   returning seat that is in the roster with chips signs the hand it adopts at stage 0 and is dealt in as a member, because there is
   no return certificate at two seats and the one other seat is the whole table: what it plays for is what the other seat's copy
   names, and disputing that is D-007's territory -- leaving.
4. **Both seats stay required at two seats.** The first heads-up run (`run080025-2`) had the survivor's next hand require a
   seat that had *taken part*, so one missed hand left the table with no next hand to deal. There is no table without both
   seats and no certificate to say one is absent, so both seats with chips stay required whatever a hand heard from them: a
   seat that stopped is waited for at stage 0, the hand is given up on the stage's budget and opened again, and a client that
   comes back finds a hand to sign.
5. **A hand nothing was dealt in is given up when the other seat has opened the next one from that give-up.** After a
   thirty-second line outage (`run080531-2`) the two seats were one hand apart and chased each other for the rest of the run:
   one gave hand k up on the budget and opened k+1, the other finished k's stage 0 late from the re-sent copy, and each then
   gave its hand up after the other had moved on. No chips are at stake before the deal, an abort's terminal follows from the
   genesis (`Hand::genesis_if_given_up`), and the other seat's `HAND_INIT` names the parent it opened at -- so a seat inside
   an undealt hand that sees the next one opened at exactly its own give-up gives up too, and the two open the same hand.
   Heads-up only, where the other seat is the whole table; with certificates the aborts are shared.
6. **A hand both seats have signed keeps a longer stage budget, heads-up.** One seat's line cut for thirty seconds
   (`run090108-2`): the seat gave the hand up on the ordinary budget (`crypto_step_timeout_ms`, 30 s) while the other had dealt
   it and waited for an action; the survivor holds a give-up from the other seat until its own deadline (§4.10), which for a
   dealt hand is the hand deadline, so the two could not meet again inside the run. Nobody can vote at two seats, so a
   stage budget's only effect there is a unilateral give-up, and the carrier repairs a brief outage by itself within
   `CARRIER_GIVES_UP_MS`: a hand both seats have signed is given up on `HEADS_UP_STAGE_BUDGET_MS` = 100 000 instead. A hand
   the other seat never signed -- stage 0, the hand a returning seat is waited for in -- keeps the ordinary budget, which is
   point 4's road. The one-machine harness's `-LinkDown` models a carrier that forgets what arrived while the line was down
   (its own doc says so), so it cannot show the repair; the repair is the group's own, measured under `S1-CM`.
7. **The returning seat adopts the running hand as a member.** `run085603-2` (the opponent's client stopped at a hand open):
   the survivor gave every waiting hand up on its budget and opened the next with both seats (point 4 held), but the returning
   seat never signed anything -- its own opening was never sent (a leftover of the bystander road, where the adopter signs
   nothing), a live hand could not be adopted at all (the pick wanted a later frame of the hand, and a hand waiting at stage 0
   for the returning seat has none), and an adopted hand the survivor had given up was never abandoned for the newer one. At
   two seats now: the one other seat's opening alone is enough to adopt, the returning seat is a member and its opening goes
   out, and a member's adopted hand in which nothing was dealt is abandoned for a newer hand the other seat has opened.
8. **What this does not do:** end a dealt hand stuck on an absent seat before the table's hand deadline (`S1-CZ`); or say
   anything heads-up that a certificate says at three seats.

**Guard.** `app` (two tests), `storage::session` (one), `table::hand` (`Opening::adopt`'s test, rewritten for the majority of the
others; `heads_up_a_seat_that_stopped_is_still_required_next_hand`, `heads_up_a_returning_seat_adopts_the_running_hand_as_a_member`,
`heads_up_a_survivors_give_up_ends_the_adopted_hand_at_this_clients_deadline`, `heads_up_a_signed_hand_keeps_the_longer_stage_budget`),
and the runs named in the `S1-CX` row.

## D-032 — three returns and no more

**Built 2026-09-11 at the project owner's instruction**, in the owner's words: *every opponent may come back to an unfinished
game three times; after the next, fourth, absence they are out, so that nobody holds a game up with it.*

1. **The count.** `MAX_RETURNS` = 3. At three seats or more a return is a certificate (`S1-BM`, D-028), the one shared record of
   a seat coming back, and every seat counts them hand to hand in its `Opening` (`returns`, carried like `grace`, this
   receiver's own). At the limit a client votes for no further return of that seat, says so once per hand, and a certificate
   needs every voter -- so one refusal keeps the seat out, and a voter whose count is short (a restarted client counts from
   zero) changes nothing. The seat stays what a certified-absent seat is: the tournament's dead seat, which posts its blinds
   and drains (D-023, `PROTOCOL.md` §8.3). No new power: nobody removes anybody; the table declines to readmit --
   **until D-047** (2026-09-12): the fourth absence puts the seat out of the table and of its group for good.
2. **Heads-up.** No certificate at two seats (D-007). The other seat's client counts the absences it asked about -- an
   episode of `OPPONENT_GONE_MS` or longer that ended with the opponent back -- and at the fourth such absence the question
   is final: *three returns are the limit, the game ends here*, with leaving the one thing offered; a headless client leaves at
   once. That is D-007's remedy taken, not a new one: the survivor may always leave, and here it does.
3. **What this does not do.** Count across the counting client's own restart (a resumed client counts from zero, which at
   three seats or more only makes its vote a yes among the others' refusals); tell the refused seat why (its client sees the
   table decline and, in time, its stack drain); or measure the rule on the bed, whose harness drops a seat once per run --
   the engine and the app carry the tests.

**Guard.** `table::hand::three_returns_are_the_limit`, `app::a_heads_up_opponent_may_return_three_times`.

## D-033 — a player back before the hand's time limit plays the interrupted hand out

**Built 2026-09-11 at the project owner's instruction**, in the owner's words: *a player whose client stopped comes back into the
hand they were in and plays it out, if they are back before that hand's time limit; when that cannot be done safely, they fold.*

1. **What a restart loses, and what is kept from here on.** A hand's deck key is drawn fresh for every hand and lived in the
   process that stopped; without it a seat can neither read its own two cards nor help open the board. The client now keeps the
   running hand's key in its session record on its own disk, beside the identity key, from the moment the deck stage begins
   (`Record` v3: `hand_secret` and the hand it belongs to; `HandSecret::keep` / `kept`; the vendored ziffle's
   `SecretKey::to_bytes` / `from_bytes` / `public_key`). No message carries it, and the record of the finished hand drops it.
2. **The table says the hand again.** The engine keeps every frame it accepted this hand (`Hand::transcript`); when a ratification
   copy arrives after the table was set -- a seat back from a restart -- the survivor says the running hand's frames again over
   the group, its own with them, at most once in five seconds.
3. **The returning client takes the hand up where it stood.** A copy of its own opening among the table's copies means its
   previous life signed the hand, so the hand is not opened anew: `Hand::open_restoring` makes and hears no opening, takes this
   seat's old frames from the wire like anybody's, and gives the deck stage the kept key (or a fresh one it never uses, when
   none was kept); the client replays the frames, and `restore_done` makes whatever the current stage still wants from the
   seat -- a deck key of its own if the table never had one, a shuffle, a commitment, its shares, its word at a showdown.
   With the key it reads the same two cards and plays on; the engine's test plays such a hand out to one settlement on both
   sides.
4. **Without the key, the fold.** A hand with no kept key, or another hand's, can be followed and folded, not played out: no
   share of the seat's is made, its cards are not read, at a showdown it mucks, and the node folds at the seat's turn. Heads-up
   the fold ends the hand; at three seats or more a board the seat cannot help open waits for the certificate road, as before.
5. **The time limit is the survivor's, unchanged.** A dealt hand in a betting stage waits for `hand_deadline_ms` (about
   eighteen minutes at two seats); a hand in a deck stage for `HEADS_UP_STAGE_BUDGET_MS`. A client back before that plays on;
   one back after it is dealt into the next hand (D-031).
6. **Measured.** `run105747-2` found the transcript empty (each accepted frame was opened against the slot after the dispatch
   had moved it on) -- the transcript is keyed by the frame's bytes since. `run110811-2` (heads-up, the client stopped at
   its turn one second after the deal, before the record had the key): the survivor said the hand's sixteen frames again,
   the returning client took the hand up from both openings, replayed fourteen frames, knew it had no key, folded at its
   turn, and the hand was over on both sides at once -- the next hands followed at the ordinary cadence, no hundred-second
   give-up. `run111821-3` (three seats, the seat stopped at its turn, the record holding the key): the founder said the hand's twenty frames again, the returning client took the hand up with its key, played it out itself, and no certificate was needed -- thirty-one hands.
   Heads-up, `run135015-2` (2026-09-11, `-Seats 2 -DropAt 150 -DropFor 20 -DropOnTurn`): the seat stopped at its turn
   in hand #20, was back 20 s later, adopted the hand with its kept key and ended it 0.7 s after the adoption; hand #21
   opened at one genesis on both and 69 hands followed with no disagreement. The survivor said the hand again twice
   (point 2's re-say, at 178.6 s and 238.7 s) and asked D-034's question at 191.7 s.

7. **What this does not do.** Keep a key past its hand (the record holds one hand's); protect a client that stopped before
   the deck stage's first frame reached it (fold-only then); or say anything at three seats or more that the certificates
   do not already say.

**Guard.** `table::hand::a_member_comes_back_into_a_dealt_hand_with_its_secret_and_plays_it_out`,
`table::hand::a_member_back_without_its_secret_can_only_fold`, `storage::session` (the record round-trips), and the runs named
in the `S1-CZ` row.

**Amended 2026-09-15 (`S1-FT`, `S1-FS`).** Point 1's key went into the record at every deck stage but one: the first hand at a client's next table when the previous table had been left inside its own first hand -- the node's table slot still held that the record had hand #1's key -- and a restart inside that hand came back without its key. And point 4's fold was said as a clock that ran out and sat the player out (`D-049`) whenever the own clock reached the turn before the fold's own tick did. The fold of a seat without its key is this rule's and sits nobody out. **Guard.** `net::run::back_at_the_table::a_slot_forgets_every_table_field_when_it_leaves_the_table`.

**Amended 2026-09-16 (`S1-FU`).** Point 3's hand taken up is said to the window from its start: `HandBegan` before the board, the table state and the turn, the cards after them -- on the stall tick's road as on an incoming frame's. The window keeps nothing about a hand it does not hold, and a hand taken up at a turn had shown no board and no turn to act on until the next frame from the table said its start.

## D-034 — thirty seconds to decide

**Built 2026-09-11 at the project owner's instruction**, from the owner's observation at the window: the thirty seconds on
the clock ran out and the forced fold came much later. It did: the client's own tables advertised 20 s to act, 5 s of grace
and a 30 s reserve, so the table's certificate could fold a seat only after 55 s (measured at about 58 s after a stop,
`run090510-3`), while the window's clock ran over the 20 s alone.

1. **The numbers.** `DECISION_MS` = 30 000 to act, `DECISION_GRACE_MS` = 3 000 for the network, no reserve, on every table
   this client hosts (`src/net/run.rs`'s advert). The window's clock is the thirty seconds; the fold follows within the grace
   and a vote's round trip. The rated preset (`RATED_SNG_POKERTH_V1`) keeps its own numbers, which §13 fixes.
   **Amended 2026-09-11 evening, on the owner's question** (*every seat folds for itself at its own thirty seconds; the
   others force it only if that does not come*): the seat's own client checks or folds for it at the timeout plus what is
   left of its reserve -- the clock the window shows -- and not at the grace's end. `Hand::action_deadline` added the grace
   too, so the own fold went out at 33 s, after the others' clocks (which start a delivery earlier) had run out, and raced
   their vote instead of landing before it; the grace stays where it belongs, in `next_deadline_for` for the others'
   judgement. Test: `a_seats_own_clock_is_its_timeout_and_reserve_and_not_the_grace`.
   **Amended twice more the same night, on the owner's second finding** (S1-DM: the fold still came late). First,
   the preset: point 1 above had reached `new_table` alone, and `TableAd::sng` -- the window's Sit & Go and the
   headless `--host` -- still dealt 20 s to act, 5 s of grace and a 30 s reserve, so the first slow decision took
   50 s and every one after it 20 s (`split201510-3`). Every Sit & Go but the rated preset now carries `DECISION_MS`,
   `DECISION_GRACE_MS` and no reserve. Second, the origin: the thirty seconds are counted from the moment the turn
   was GIVEN -- the stamp of the action, deal or board that gave it, on its emitter's clock -- and not from the moment
   each client heard of it. The acting seat's own clock (`Clock::Start { began_unix_ms }`) and every felt's
   countdown (`elapsed_ms` on `YourTurn` and `NotYourTurn`) start there, so a late delivery no longer adds itself
   twice; the own clock never runs past the timeout and never under half a second, and an unknown or future stamp
   means the plain timeout. `split203531-3`, every seat thinking past its clock: every seat's own client acted 29.6-30.1 s after its *your turn* (the founder 150.1 to 179.7 s and 210.1 to 239.7 s, the joiner 87.1 to 116.7 s and 236.6 to 266.5 s, the far seat 118.4 to 148.5 s, 178.4 to 208.4 s and 268.4 to 298.4 s), where `split201510-3` had read 49.7-50.0 s once and 20 s after.
2. **Heads-up, the same question.** Nobody can fold for anybody at two seats (D-007). A present opponent past their time and
   the question's own wait (`OPPONENT_GONE_MS`) is asked about with the one question the window has -- *wait, or leave* --
   said as what it is: *on the clock for N s, past their 30 s to decide*. The episode ends when they act; it is no absence and
   no return (D-032).
3. **What this does not do.** Fold anybody heads-up, or change the rated preset.

**Guard.** `app::a_slow_heads_up_opponent_is_asked_about_and_the_question_ends_when_they_act`; the corpus gate on the two
constants.

**Amended 2026-09-15 (`S1-FS`, the owner: *"po obnovení handy po reconnectu je klient v režimu sit out a musím stisknout I'm back"*).** The thirty seconds run from when the turn was given, and never from before the player could see it. A turn that already stood when a restarted client took its hand up again (`D-033`) is given, to that life of the client, at the take-up: the player has the whole clock from there. A turn heard with less than ten seconds of its time left (`LATE_TURN_LEFT_MS`) -- a line that was down; heads-up nobody folds for the seat meanwhile (`D-007`) -- has ten seconds from when it was heard. A delivery any less late still takes its seconds out of the thirty, so the fold lands where the other windows' countdowns end, as point 1 says; the window's own countdown starts at the same instant as the own clock. **Guard.** `net::run::back_at_the_table`, `table::hand::tests::a_turn_says_when_it_was_given_and_when_this_client_could_show_it`.

**Amended 2026-09-16 (`S1-FX`).** Heads-up, an opponent that comes back on the line to its own turn is counted from its return -- its client, back from a restart, took the hand up with its whole clock -- and point 2's question about a present opponent past its time follows that count. Asked from the turn's stamp, it opened the moment the opponent was back, over a clock drawn empty.

## D-035 — a seat that left the table's group is gone, and the link is the group's

**Built 2026-09-11 at the project owner's instruction**, from the owner's finding at the window: an opponent who had left
the table stayed on the felt with cards, a stack and a *0 ms* ping. The ping was the lobby's -- libp2p's, to a client that
was merely still running -- and the table's carrier, its Tox group, which knew the seat had gone, told nobody: `LeaveTable`
drops the group and says nothing on the wire, `PLAYER_LEAVE` is a boundary-window event nobody reads, and the roster keeps
every seat a table has (D-022).

1. **The carrier reports departures.** The group's peer-exit callback reads the leaving peer's group key while the peer still
   exists and whether it *quit* (`TOX_GROUP_EXIT_TYPE_QUIT`) as against timing out; the driver maps the key through
   `known_as` to the seat's application key (`S1-I`) and hands the node `(seat, quit)`; every sweep it also publishes the set of
   roster seats that are confirmed members right now.
2. **The link is the group's.** Once the hand rides the group, a lobby ping is sent to the window only for a seat that is a
   confirmed member; a seat that left gets a reading of `None` at once and no readings after, so the window's link goes
   stale rather than green.
3. **The window.** `SeatLeft` marks the seat gone: drawn dim, *left the table* where its cards were, no clock; a reading from
   the group again un-marks it. Heads-up a **quit** ends the game -- the question window says *your opponent left the table;
   the game is over* with leaving the one thing offered, and a headless client leaves; a **timeout** is an absence the seat
   may come back from (D-031, D-032), and counts as one.
4. **What this does not do.** Change the roster or any chip: a seat that quit keeps its place in the roster the protocol
   derives (D-022), and at three seats or more the certificates treat it as the absent seat it is; nor end a hand the
   quitter left unsettled before its deadline (heads-up the survivor leaves; D-033's roads are for a client that comes
   back).

**Guard.** `app::a_seat_that_left_the_group_is_gone_and_heads_up_a_quit_ends_the_game`.

**Amended 2026-09-15, the owner's word (`S1-FQ`)** (*"ten game is over s opponent left musí být prokazatelně, když
poslední soupeř aktivně opustí stůl"*). Point 3's *heads-up a quit ends the game* is withdrawn. The carrier's *quit* is
said of a client that merely rejoins the group -- toxcore's `gc_rejoin_group` sends the peer-exit first, and so do a
founder yielding its own copy of the group (`S1-FE`) and the driver giving up a stalled join -- and the owner's test,
a heads-up founder killed and started again twice, was told *your opponent left the table, the game is over*. A player
who leaves says so: `TABLE_LEAVE` (`PROTOCOL.md` §7.10), signed by its seat's key for the table and sent over the
group before its client leaves it; the window says *your opponent left the table* on that word alone, at once, and only
when that seat was the last other one in the game. The group's goodbye marks the seat gone from the felt as a timeout
does, and the table's removal of a seat (`D-047`, `D-051`) is for good but no leave. **Guard.**
`app::tests::only_the_seats_own_word_is_a_player_leaving`,
`a_seat_that_left_the_group_is_gone_and_heads_up_only_its_own_word_ends_the_game`,
`net::tabletalk::tests::a_leave_word_is_heard_only_from_its_seat_for_its_table`.


## D-036 — several seats quiet at one stage are certified together, and the voters must outnumber them

**Decided 2026-09-11 on the project owner's ruling** (*no deadlocks in the game; the game safe; the mechanism not open to
misuse, and whoever misuses it is put out without compromise*), from `S1-CT`: three seats quiet at one cryptographic stage
could never be certified, each being a voter about the other two, and the table stood -- with `S1-CW` fixed it would have
ended every hand on the deadline with the same nine seats and shed nobody.

1. **One certificate names the whole quiet set.** A `TIMEOUT_VOTE` still names one seat. A `TIMEOUT_CERT` names a set `S`
   of seats quiet at one stage under one deadline and carries, for every seat of `S`, a vote from every seat of `V(S)` =
   the dealt-in seats less `S` less the seats a completed certificate earlier in the hand already names; its digest
   commits to the whole set. One seat is D-023's certificate exactly, digest and bytes alike.
2. **The floor has two halves.** `|V(S)| >= 2` as before (D-008), and `|V(S)| > |S|`: the voters outnumber the seats
   named, so no group short of a majority of the live seats completes a certificate about the rest. Where the quiet are
   half the live seats or more no certificate forms, no vote is cast, and the hand ends on its deadline naming nobody, as
   §8.4 always said. At three seats with two quiet that is the whole-hand limit, as before. **The window says so** (S1-DI,
   2026-09-11 evening): once per hand, the seats that stopped, how many are present to vote, and that the table waits
   for them -- wait, or leave.
3. **Being voted against is still not exclusion.** `S` leaves `V(S)` only inside the certificate that unanimously names
   every member of it; a vote about a seat removes it from nothing. The rule §8.4 deleted under D-008 let one client
   shrink `V` by assertion; this lets nobody shrink it by less than the word of everybody outside the set.
4. **What a group can do with it, and what a seat pays.** At a cryptographic stage a certificate ends the hand and moves
   no chip (D-010); the seats named leave `R(k+1)` and come back only by D-028's return, which D-032 counts -- three
   returns and no more. A group of `n - k` seats can name `k`, which is the power it always had to leave the table and
   play without them; a seat that goes quiet to void a hand pays with a return, and the fourth absence is final. That is
   the owner's kick, and it is the same kick for one quiet seat and for three.
5. **How the sealer finds the set.** The greatest set `S` of seats voted about at this stage such that every seat of
   `V(S)` has voted about every member of `S` (`Hand::sealable_set`). Sealable sets are closed under union, so every
   honest seat converges on one `S` as the votes reach it. A certificate carries its votes, so a receiver that lacks one
   holds it from the copy and seals the same set; a copy about a smaller set is answered by this client's own about the
   larger, which carries the votes that prove it, and the certificate stage moves with the set. One strike per seat per
   stage, however many sets name it. A seat named by others does not seal: the subject accepts a certificate naming it
   and never emits one.
6. **What this does not do.** Change the vote, the betting-stage certificate (`kind = 1` names the one seat to act),
   D-007 (nothing at two seats) or the hand deadline. It does not make a lying voter provable (Q-08 stands), and it
   does not shed seats that are half the table or more -- `D-066` (2026-09-18) does: exactly half holding the lowest
   seat, and any two after five minutes out of the table's group.
7. **Measured.** In the engine, tests first and seen red: `seats_quiet_together_at_one_stage_are_certified_together_and_the_hand_ends`
   (five seats, two quiet: three copies, both named, the next hand at one genesis without them),
   `a_joint_certificate_needs_the_voters_to_outnumber_the_quiet` (two present, three quiet: no vote, the deadline),
   `a_peer_copy_carries_the_votes_this_client_lacks_and_it_seals_the_same_set`; `a_joint_certificate_at_its_widest_fits_its_cap`
   (four named by six, twenty-four votes, 12 459 B; `TIMEOUT_CERT_CAP` raised from 8 192 to 13 312); the fourteen of
   `tests/timeout_certificate.rs`, one rewritten to the carried votes. **On the bed, `run145004-5`** (`tools/table-run.ps1
   -Seats 5 -Seconds 420 -DropAt 60 -DropAtOpen -DropFor 600 -DropNodes 1,2`, the harness's new `-DropNodes`: two joiners
   stop at the open of the same hand and stay away): n1 and n2 stopped at the open of hand #3 at 61-62 s; the three
   survivors' clocks ran out at stage 0 between 90 and 96 s, each voted about both, and each sealed *the table has certified
   seats [1, 2]'s timeout, unanimously among [0, 3, 4]* within 1.5 s of the others (n4 91.6 s, n3 92.3 s, n0 97.0 s on
   their own clocks); hand #3 ended at all three, the roster went `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4] -> [0, 3, 4]`, and hand #4 opened at
   one genesis with three seats on all three -- 45 hands in the run, no disagreement, 8.3 s a hand. The tally's
   denominator read *3/4 agree* on a certificate that had just completed among three (the single-subject count); it
   now counts the voters of the whole quiet set (`tally_need`). **On the split bed, `split151655-9`** (`tools/table-run-split.ps1
   -Here 8 -There 1 -Seconds 480 -StopAtOpen 90 -StopSeats 3,5,7`, the split harness's new knob: those local seats stop at
   their first hand open at or after 90 s and stay away; the far seat, relay-only, is seat 1 and a voter): two of the three
   -- seats 7 and 8 -- stopped at the open of hand #1 (their own clocks 90.1 s and 95.3 s), the third had opened hand #1
   just under its 90 s and stopped at hand #2's open instead. Hand #1: the seven others' clocks ran out at stage 0, the
   tally climbed to 7/7 on both subjects, and every one of the seven -- the far seat among them, its vote and its copy
   across the far link -- sealed *the table has certified seats [7, 8]'s timeout, unanimously among [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]*
   (founder 132.9 s, far seat 131.4 s); hand #1 ended, the roster went to seven, hand #2 opened at one genesis. Hand #2:
   seat 3 alone, certified among the six as D-023 always did; hand #3 opened with `[0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6]` at one genesis and
   24 hands were opened on every survivor, 23 finished, no disagreement. The shape of `split162332-9` -- three quiet at
   one stage of a nine-seat table -- therefore ends in one certificate where it used to stand for the run.

**Guard.** The four engine tests above and `tests/timeout_certificate.rs`.

**Amended 2026-09-17 (`D-063`).** Point 2's floor is asked of the seats named without their player's own signed leave;
a seat named with its word counts for nothing against it, and is out of the table for good.


## D-037 — the founder records its table and comes back to it

**Built 2026-09-11 on the project owner's word** (the founder's client should know after a restart that it had a table in
play), reversing D-029 point 1, which gave the founder no record because its table could not be rejoined.

1. **The founder's record.** The session record (version 4) carries, for the founder, the table key's seed and the last
   `PLAYER_LIST` it signed; a seat that joined carries zeros and nothing there. Written at the moment the table is set and
   at every boundary, as for any seat.
2. **The road back.** `ResumeSession` on a founder's record rebuilds the formation from the founder's own list, checked
   against the table key as any joiner checks a list (`Formation::found_back`); the founder holds the roster, its seat 0
   and the table key again, and answers joins as before -- *already seated* to a seat that comes back, *advert expired* to
   a stranger. A set table is not advertised again.
3. **The group, from a member.** The founder's Tox key is in its profile, so the members still hold its friendship. Tox
   starts in the new role `Back` with the roster's keys as friends; every member offers the group when the founder's
   friendship comes back up, and again every sweep while its key is not a confirmed member (bounded like the founder's own
   invitations); the founder takes any member's invitation into the group the advertisement named and no other.
4. **The session and the hand, like any returning seat.** In the group with a roster and no session the founder says its
   recorded ratification again (D-029 point 7), the members answer with theirs, the session is the table's (D-029 point 8),
   the running hand is adopted from the members' copies and the seat comes back by D-028's certificate or heads-up by
   D-031's adoption; D-032 counts the return.
5. **What this does not do.** Give the founder any power it did not have: it comes back as a seat, by the same certificate
   as any seat, and moves no chip. Nor does it answer joins while it is away -- a seat that restarts while the founder is
   away waits for the founder's return, then asks again (D-029's give-up still applies).
6. **Measured.** `net::formation::the_founder_comes_back_from_its_own_record` (rebuilt from the record, the recorded
   ratification byte for byte, the table's session from the members' copies, a seated peer answered as the founder);
   `storage::session` round trip. **On the bed, `run163147-3`** (`tools/table-run.ps1 -Seats 3 -Seconds 600 -DropAt 60
   -DropAtOpen -DropFor 20 -DropNodes 0`): the founder wrote its record at the table's setting and at every boundary,
   stopped at the open of hand #3 at 60.3 s, and the two others certified seat 0 out at 88.9 s and played hands #4 and #5
   between them; its new process, 20 s later, read the record (*rejoining ... as its founder*), was in the group on a
   member's invitation 15.1 s after its start, had the table's session at 18.3 s from the members' answers, adopted hand #5
   as a bystander at 20.3 s, asked to sit in at that hand's boundary, was voted back 2/2 (*the roster of hand #6 is
   re-derived*) and was back in the roster from hand #6 on -- opened at one genesis on all three, 25.5 s into its new
   life; 70 hands in the run, 66 of them at the returned founder, no disagreement. The first attempt (`run160631-3`)
   wrote no record at all: the record's gate read `joined_key` alone, and was widened to the founder; the second
   (`run162048-3`) formed no group on the bed and measured nothing.

**Guard.** The formation test above, `storage::session` (the record), and the run named in point 6.

**Amended 2026-09-15 (`S1-FR`, the owner: *"ten deadlock musí být odstraněn"*).** Point 3 has the members offer the group to the founder back, and point 5 leaves a seat that restarts *while the founder is away* to wait for the founder's return -- but a seat that restarted after the founder was back waited for an invitation nobody would send: the founder back offered the group to no one, and heads-up its copy was the only one left. The founder back now offers the group as the founder does -- the invitation sweep, and the re-offer to a roster friend whose friendship comes back up -- once it holds a settled copy of the group it joined. Still open: when every client that holds a copy of the group restarts before one of them is back (heads-up, both), no copy is left -- a Tox profile keeps the client's key and not its groups -- and nobody can offer one. **Guard.** `tox::table::tests::a_founder_back_in_the_group_offers_it_and_a_member_does_not`.

## D-038 — a seat on a hand nobody else has rejoins the table from its copies

**Built 2026-09-11, evening**, from `S1-DH`: after a 70 s outage a live client latched itself out of a table that had
gone on without it and dealt nothing for the rest of the run (`run172000-3`), and the latch tripped on two seats' word,
which in `split111706-9` put six healthy seats out of nine. The owner's standing priority applies: the game must not
deadlock, and a seat that stopped is removed by the table (D-036) -- but a seat that is there, on the line and behind
through no fault the table can name, was being left at a table it could no longer see.

1. **The table is a strict majority of the seats still in the game.** This client is *behind* when a strict majority of
   the seats in its own `required` and `returned` sets, other than itself, have signed hands two or more ids past the
   hand it holds (`ADRIFT_MARGIN`, two hands: one hand of skew is the showdown pause). A seat outside those sets -- one
   this client certified out, or a stranger -- counts for nothing however far it has got, and two seats are not the
   table. Heads-up the one other seat is the table.
2. **Behind is a return, not a terminus.** A client that finds itself behind drops the hand it holds and every local
   fact of the branch -- the retained hand, a pending repair, the next hand's buffers, the boundary windows, its own
   frames of that hand in the re-send list, a freeze -- and keeps the table, the group, the session and its keys. From
   there it takes D-029's road for a seat back from a restart (`S1-CR`): it adopts the table's running hand from a
   strict majority of the members' copies as a bystander, follows it, asks to sit in at its settled boundary (D-028),
   and is a deriving member again from the certificate on; heads-up it adopts as D-031 says. D-032 counts the return.
3. **What the table loses: nothing.** No other seat signed a frame of the dropped branch, or the branch would be the
   table; the client's checkpoint for the last shared hand went out before the latch, so nobody waited on it. The
   client's own actions on the branch are void, as they always were.
4. **What is kept ahead of time.** Copies of hands past this client's -- `HAND_INIT`s and the frames beside them --
   are stashed whether or not the client is resuming (two hand ids, one copy per seat, `RESUME_EARLY_CAP` other frames),
   so the adoption has its evidence the moment the latch fires rather than a hand later.
5. **What this does not do.** Give the seat any power: it comes back by the same certificate as any seat, moves no chip,
   and a table with no majority at one genesis is still one it waits at. Nor does it settle who was right -- `S1-CE`,
   `S1-CN` and `S1-CI` keep their questions; this bounds what the answer costs a player.
6. **Measured.** `net::run::a_minority_two_hands_ahead_is_not_the_table_and_a_majority_is` (two of eight and four of
   eight do not move the table, five do, strangers never, heads-up the other seat does). **On the bed, `run173830-3`**
   (`tools/table-run.ps1 -Seats 3 -Seconds 600 -LinkDownAt 60 -LinkDownFor 70 -LinkDownNode 1`, the same shape as the
   baseline `run172000-3`): seat 1's line went down at 60 s; the two others certified it out at 120.3 s and played on;
   seat 1 opened hand #8 alone during the outage. The line came back at 130 s, and at 138.6 s seat 1 said *this client
   is on a hand nobody else has: the table is at hand #10 and this client reached only hand #8* -- 0.1 s later it had
   adopted hand #10 as a bystander from the two copies already stashed (15 frames replayed), at 139.2 s it asked to
   sit in, and at 144.2 s it was *back in the roster from hand #11 on* on a 2/2 return vote: 14 s from the line's
   return to the roster, three hands lost (#8 to #10) against the whole rest of the run before. 58 hands at the table,
   54 at seat 1, one genesis on all three for every hand but seat 1's private #8; the harness reads it as
   BEHIND-REJOINED rather than ADRIFT.

**Guard.** The test in point 6, the S1-DH row, and the run named in point 6.

## D-039 — a seat the table's copies deal in adopts the running hand as a member

**Built 2026-09-11, evening**, from `S1-DJ`: two seats of four restarted together and never came back -- the present two
could certify nobody (D-036), every hand waited at stage 0 for the missing copies and ended on its budget, and the
returning seats adopted each such hand as bystanders and asked to sit in at boundaries that, being aborted, readmit
nobody (`S1-R`). The table was waiting for exactly the two copies the returning seats were not allowed to make.

1. **The required set of an adopted hand.** D-029 took the copies' signers as `R(k)`, exact only when every required
   seat's copy had come. The copies' body carries the table's own word on who plays the hand -- `HAND_INIT`'s
   `dealt_in`, signed by a strict majority of the other seats, and `dealt_in ⊆ R(k)` (§4.4) -- so the required set is
   now **the body's `dealt_in` joined with the signers**: still a subset of `R(k)`, and exact whenever every required seat
   is dealt in, which is every hand this client can open (a required seat outside `dealt_in` has no chips or no grace,
   and nothing here emits a sit-out).
2. **A seat the table deals in is a member.** It opens the adopted hand anew at the table's genesis and says its
   `HAND_INIT`: the same body, byte for byte, under its own signature -- the copy the table's stage 0 was waiting for.
   Its previous life's copy among the table's (D-033) still means *taken up where it stood* instead; the node tells the
   two apart by the signers. A seat the body does not deal in is a bystander as before, and it waits for stage 0 to
   close elsewhere (every copy in, or a later frame seen) before it follows, saying once why.
3. **A hand nothing was dealt in is abandoned for the table's newer one** when a majority has opened it, at any table
   size -- S1-CX's heads-up rule generalised. A table that gave hand `k` up on its budget while this seat was adopting
   it has opened `k+1`; the seat adopts that one as a member within a tick, and stage 0 closes on the two copies within
   its budget.
4. **What this does not do.** Readmit anybody: a seat outside `dealt_in` -- certified out, busted, out of grace -- is
   a bystander and comes back by D-028's certificate as before. Nor does it derive anything: the genesis, the button,
   the blinds and the stacks are the copies', as D-029 says.
5. **Measured.** `table::hand::a_seat_the_tables_copies_deal_in_adopts_as_a_member_and_signs_the_same_body`; the
   heads-up adoption tests read the survivor's word. **On the bed**, the baseline `run175510-4` again with the
   harness's new `-DropAtHand 5` (`tools/table-run.ps1 -Seats 4 -Seconds 480 -DropAtHand 5 -DropFor 40 -DropNodes
   "1,2"`; `-DropAtOpen` counts seconds from each process's own start and put the two stops on different hands in
   `run180731-4`). `run182312-4`: both stopped at the open of hand #5 at 61 s; the present two ended #5 and #6 on the
   stage-0 budget, saying S1-DI's line; the two new processes, 40 s later, *resumed at hand #7 as a member ... this seat
   signed it and is dealt in* 24 s into their lives, the table's stage 0 closed on their copies and hand #7 was dealt to
   all four -- and then seat 3 was certified out of it: its stage 0 had closed on the copies applied inside the
   adoption, whose `on_event` answer (the deck stage's contribution) the node dropped, while seat 1's closed on a copy
   that came through the ordinary road and its contribution went out. Fixed (a member's adoption says what the copies'
   `on_event` returns; the test asserts the last copy returns it) and measured again: `run183451-4`, the same command: both stopped at the open of hand #5, the present two ended #5, #6 and #7 on the stage-0 budget with S1-DI's line, the two new processes *resumed at hand #8 as a member ... this seat signed it and is dealt in*, hand #8 was dealt to all four and both were *back in the roster from hand #9 on* at its boundary -- **no certificate anywhere in the run**, 42 hands, one genesis on all four (10.1 s per hand in the steady state).

**Guard.** The test in point 5, the S1-DJ row, and the run named in point 5.

## D-040 — the lobby is asked, not only overheard

**Built 2026-09-11, evening**, from `S1-DK`: the owner's second client on the same machine listed the player and not the
open table, and the morning's bed had formed no table four runs running. The founder had never been told the other
client was on the lobby topic -- GossipSub says so once, with the first connection, and the first connection between
two clients on one machine is not always one that carries it -- so its advert had nobody to go to. §7.5 already
specified a snapshot RPC for a newly joined client; nothing had built it.

1. **The question.** §7.5's `LOBBY_SNAPSHOT_REQUEST`, a signed event over `/p2p-poker/lobby-snapshot/1` with the
   RPC's own length-prefixed framing (as the join RPC; the corpus said `request_response::cbor` and now says this),
   asked of every poker peer the moment `identify` names it one of us and again every `AD_REBROADCAST_MS` while it is
   connected, under a fresh nonce each time.
2. **The answer.** `LOBBY_SNAPSHOT_RESPONSE` under the question's nonce: the founder's own advert while its table is
   open (a table that has dealt is not offered, D-037 and §7.3), nothing otherwise. One answer per peer in five
   seconds; a question the responder cannot read goes unanswered. The asker takes each advert through §7.2's
   checklist exactly as one heard over gossip -- **the responder is not trusted for anything** -- and tells the window
   `TableSeen` as before, with a log line naming the road (*heard by asking*) when the question carried it first.
3. **The withdrawal.** A table the asker lists whose `founder_peer_id` is the answering peer and which the answer does
   not name is removed at once (`TableGone`): the founder is the authority on what it offers. A closed table leaves
   every lobby at the next question, within thirty seconds, instead of at `AD_TTL_MS`; the TTL stays for a founder
   that vanished without answering, which is a founder that may come back (D-037).
4. **What this does not do.** Replace the mesh -- adverts still ride it, and where it works a table appears in
   seconds either way -- or hand anybody a power: an answer can omit a table (the asker asks the founder itself) and
   cannot invent, alter or prolong one. Nor does it repair the library's exchange; `S1-G`'s reading of it stands.
5. **Measured.** `net::snapshot` (a question and its answer round trip under the nonce; the refusals, one rule at a
   time), `app::a_table_its_founder_withdrew_leaves_the_screen_at_once`. **On the bed**, with the harness's new
   `-NoJoin` (every node but the founder watches the lobby and joins nothing, so the table stays open) and
   `-LeaveTableAt` (`tools/table-run.ps1 -Seats 3 -NoJoin -LeaveTableAt 60 -Seconds 120`), read with
   `tools/fold-lobby.py`. `run193224-3`: both watchers listed the table **0.1 s** into their lives, *heard by asking*,
   while the founder's own status line read *0 of 2 subscribed peers grafted* for the whole run -- the mesh had not
   grafted them and the question did not care; the founder left at 62.2 s and both watchers withdrew the table at
   their next question, about a second later (their clocks run two seconds behind the founder's). The two runs before
   it taught the withdrawal its two rules: in `run192317-3` a watcher's first question beat the hosting by a second
   and its empty answer withdrew a table the mesh had just delivered (rule: an answer withdraws only a table
   advertised before it, both on the founder's clock), and in `run192814-3` both watchers withdrew at 30 s on an
   answer that DID carry the advert, because the store had just taken the same copy over the mesh and refused it as
   not newer (rule: an answer names every advert it carries that verifies, whether or not the store took it). Across
   machines: `split193449-3` (two seats here, one on the far box, multicast off): the far seat reached the founder through the public lobby at 69.3 s of its life and listed the table 0.1 s later -- the founder's re-shout on its subscription arrived a second before the answer to its question (*1 table offered* at 71.0 s), so both roads carried it; once the table had dealt the founder answered *0 tables* and both other seats dropped the listing at 90-91 s, which is §7.3's withdrawal of a started table made explicit.

**Guard.** The tests in point 5, the S1-DK row, `tools/fold-lobby.py` over the runs named in point 5.

## D-041 — a seat is on the line when the table's group holds it

**Built 2026-09-11, night, on the project owner's ruling** (*the pinging of the seats at the table and the offline
reading must go through the Tox group, like the game data*), from `S1-DL`: the far seat was drawn *offline* through a
whole game, and on the far machine every opponent was, while the hand's traffic flowed over the group.

1. **The reading.** `SeatLink` carries the group's word, `group`: whether the table's Tox group holds the seat's client
   as a confirmed member right now (D-035's `present`, by application key through the `known_as` bridge, which the
   first version never filled) or, before the seat has spoken in the group, whether the friend connection to its Tox
   key is up (`friends_on`). The felt draws *on the line* from it, in green; a fresh libp2p ping adds its figure beside
   it; *offline* is drawn only when neither holds (and, on a table that does not ride Tox, when the last ping's
   connection closed, as before).
2. **When it is said.** Every stall tick the node reads each seat's word and the last ping, and tells the window on
   any change and every ten seconds regardless, so the reading never goes stale on a seat that never pings. A libp2p
   connection closing is no longer an *offline* on a Tox table; a seat that left the group is (D-035).
3. **What this does not do.** Change who is certified or when: the certificate's clocks are §8 and D-036's. The reading
   is for the player's eyes and for the heads-up question (D-032, D-034), which now asks about a seat the group has
   lost rather than one a ping has.
4. **Measured.** `app::the_chat_the_mutes_and_the_links_reach_the_window` and the heads-up tests under D-032 and D-034
   (a reading with the group's word counts as reachable). On the bed: `split203531-3` (two seats here, one on the far box): the founder read seat 1 *on the line by the table's group* from 25 s and the far seat from 273 s, but the joiner and the far seat read only each other -- the founder's own roster entry carried no Tox key (`Formation::found` wrote `None`), so its friend link could not be read at the others; fixed, and in `run204636-3` (three seats here) every seat read every other *on the line* from 16-18 s, each group member taught to its seat within the first hand.

**Guard.** The tests in point 4, the S1-DL row.

**D-035 and D-041 amended 2026-09-12 (S1-DS).** The exit's key is the one the driver remembered for the peer
when the callback cannot read it; the friend link says *on the line* only for a seat the group has not yet
taught, since a seat it has taught and does not hold now has left, and its friendship lingers (D-042); a seat
that left has no link line on the felt; and the library forgets a seat that quit (`patches/0031`). **And again the same day (S1-DT):** a member the group has heard nothing from for `QUIET_LIMIT_S` (twenty
seconds) is off the line, though the library keeps it a member for 58 s -- a client that died says nothing;
the library says how long it has been quiet (`patches/0032`). **And a third time (S1-DU):** a seat may hold several group entries -- the one
its dead client left behind for 58 s and the fresh one its restart made -- and every reader takes all of them:
presence by any confirmed entry, quiet by the freshest, and *gone* only when no confirmed entry of its remains. **And again (S1-DX, the owner's rule):** on a Tox table the felt's line is the group's alone -- no friend
link, no libp2p ping -- and the figure beside the dot is how long ago the group last heard the seat.

## D-042 — one Tox instance per client, a group per table

**Built 2026-09-12, on the project owner's rulings** (*one Tox instance per client, started with the client and not
with a table; a group per table; when a tournament ends its group is left and the friends it was played with go; up
to four tables at once*), from `S1-DN`: after a finished tournament nobody could sit at a new table without a restart
or a wait, because every table started a new Tox instance that bootstrapped from nothing and had no friend up for its
first minute.

1. **The instance.** `TableSink::boot` starts the client's one Tox instance at the node's launch, bootstrapped into
   the DHT and its relays before any table exists (the log says *tox: this client's instance is up from the start*),
   and it lives on one thread (`tox::table::Driver`) for the client's life. `start` opens a table on it, and `clear`
   closes the table and keeps the instance. A build without Tox is unchanged.
2. **A table is a group and a roster.** The driver keeps every open table: its group (created for a founder, awaited
   from an invitation otherwise), its roster of Tox keys, the `known_as` bridge, what it has invited, who is confirmed,
   what it still has to say. toxcore's events are routed by group. An invitation goes to the table still without a
   group whose advertisement named one and whose role names the inviting friend -- a joiner's founder, or for a
   founder coming back any member of its roster (D-037) -- and the group's id is read back and compared as before; a
   mismatch is left at once. A founder's invitations go to its own table's roster and to nobody else the instance
   knows.
3. **Friendships are the instance's.** Shared by every table, so a second table with the same players finds their
   links already up, which is the whole of S1-DN's minute. Closing a table says what it still held (`FLUSH_TURNS`
   turns of the loop, the other tables keeping theirs) and leaves its group; the friends no open table needs are
   dropped `FRIEND_LINGER` (two minutes) later, so the next table the same players sit at is fast and a client at the
   lobby holds no game's connections for long.
4. **The end of a tournament.** When the hand just played has no successor (*the table has no next hand to deal*),
   the node leaves the table's group `TOURNAMENT_LEAVE_GRACE` (ten seconds) later -- two rounds of the resend loop,
   so a seat that missed the terminal message hears it again before anybody is gone -- and says so (*the tournament is
   over: this client left the table's group*). The table stays on the felt until the player leaves it; the friends
   follow point 3.
5. **The founder invites one seat at a time** -- the next once the last is a confirmed member, or `INVITE_GAP` (three
   seconds) after -- from every turn of the driver's loop rather than from the up-edge and the five-second sweep. The
   warm instance exposed a race the cold one had hidden: two seats invited in the same instant each sync the group's
   peer list before the other is confirmed, so neither holds the other and neither opens the handshake, and they meet
   only when the founder's next ping (every `GC_PING_TIMEOUT`, twelve seconds) carries a peer count they do not have
   and their own sync limit has passed. Measured, `run212040-3` and `run212648-3`: both joiners of the second table
   invited in one sweep, each reading *group 1 seen/1 confirmed/2 wanted* for eighteen seconds, the table's first hand
   twenty-five seconds after the join; a first table's friend links come up a second apart and it deals five seconds
   after. A seat invited after the last is confirmed gets the last in its own sync and handshakes it at once.
6. **What this does not do yet.** The node still holds one table. The driver carries any number of them, which is
   what the owner's multitabling (four at once) needs first; the node's single-table state is the next step, and the
   window after it. Nothing in the protocol changes: what a table says, and to whom, is as D-019 has it. The headless
   `--then-join` now asks for a table the lobby already lists at once, as a player who can see it would; the
   thirty-second wait in `run202725-3` was the harness's lobby cadence and not the client's.
7. **Measured.** On the bed, three seats on one machine. `run212040-3` (`tools/table-run.ps1 -Seats 3 -RehostAt 90 -Seconds 300`, the one-instance driver alone): every client's instance was up from its start (0.1-2.5 s), the founder's second table dealt its first hand 20.5 s after the hosting (85 s in `run202725-3`), the joiners were seated at once and in its group 5 s later with *tox friends up 2* throughout -- and their first hand came 25 s after the join, which is the invitation race of point 5. `run213600-3` (`-StartStack 200 -RehostAt 120 -Seconds 330`, invitations one at a time, both tournaments ending inside the run): the first tournament ended at 38.5-42.1 s on the three seats and each left its group 10.4-11.7 s later; the second table dealt its first hand 15.4 s after the hosting, the first joiner was in its group 0.1 s after asking and dealt in 0.6 s after leaving the old table, the second in its group 5.3 s after asking (invited once the first was confirmed) and dealt in 10.3 s after; the second tournament ended at 225.6-229.3 s and each seat left its group 11.0-11.5 s later; fifteen hands opened and fifteen finished on every seat, one genesis per hand per table, no certificate. `run212648-3` (`-StartStack 300 -RehostAt 150`) caught the end-of-tournament leave on the thirty-second housekeeping tick, whose cadence missed the run's end; it is on the two-second stall tick now. The whole-stack test crosses the new driver in 53 s.

**Guard.** `tox::table::tests::an_invitation_is_owed_by_a_condition_and_not_by_an_edge` (a friend of another table
is never owed this table's group), the whole-stack test `a_whole_message_crosses_the_group_in_one_piece` (ignored by
default, needs the network; its fragment count was a stale number and is a bound now), the S1-DN row,
`tools/fold-rehost.py` over the runs named in point 7. Harness: `-StartStack` in `tools/table-run.ps1`
(`P2P_POKER_START_STACK`, fault-harness only) so a tournament ends inside a run, and the summary's genesis check
compares within a table, since a `-RehostAt` run holds two tables in one log and read a clean run as forked.

## D-043 — several tables in one client, in stages

**Decided 2026-09-12, on the project owner's ruling** (*up to four tables at once in one client -- multitabling*),
after D-042 gave the driver underneath the means to carry any number of groups. The node loop held one table in
some ninety locals, its window one table in some thirty fields, and every event and command named no table because
there was only ever one. The change is made in stages, each built, tested and measured on the bed before the next,
so that a single table never stops working while the second is being built.

1. **Stage 1 (built the same day): the node's table is one struct.** Every per-table local of `net::run`'s loop --
   the formation, the hand, what was said, the boundaries, the clocks, the flags that keep a line from being said
   twice, the Tox sink -- is a field of `TableRun`, built once by `TableRun::new` and used as `t.field`; the loop's
   macros take the table as their first argument, because a macro's bare names resolve where the macro is defined
   and not where it is used (`leave_the_table!(t)`, `hand_event!(t, h, bytes)`). The timers, the fault-harness
   knobs, the peers' pings, the lobby, the swarm and the relay state stay the loop's own: they are the client's, not
   a table's. Nothing else moves and nothing behaves differently: the transformation was mechanical (a script that
   took each local's declaration and its comment into the struct and renamed the uses), the compiler's word on it
   was nine shadowed bindings named `t`, and the bed's word is in point 4.
2. **Stage 2 (built the same day): the loop holds a vector of tables.** `tables: Vec<TableRun>`, at most
   `MAX_TABLES` (four), the first slot always there and `active` the one the window is at. Each arm of the loop
   picks its table before it touches one: a swarm event by `table_for_event` -- a gossip message or a subscription
   by its topic, a join request by the table id it names (a founder of several answers for the right one), a
   join answer by the request it answers (`join_pending`) -- and the active table for everything else; a Tox
   message by the sink it came from (`next_from_tables`, one future over every sink); the two timers, the own
   clock and the deal, by the earliest deadline among the tables, read before the select so the timers own
   their instants and borrow no table; the resend, stall and housekeeping ticks for every table in turn, the
   housekeeping's lobby questions once. The driver underneath is one `Arc` shared by every table's sink
   (`TableSink::share`). A `CreateTable` or `JoinTable` while this client sits at a table opens a new slot and
   makes it active; `LeaveTable` closes the slot when another is open. The discover tick's closed-table reading
   is every table's, and the DHT's effort follows any closed one; a founder's lobby answer offers every table
   it founded and has not dealt at. Commands and events still name no table: an `Act` goes to the active
   table, and every event reaches the window as before -- which is why stage 3 comes before a client is
   dealt at two tables at once.
3. **Stage 3 (built the same day): the window.** The node says which slot what follows is about --
   `NodeEvent::AtTable { slot, key }`, sent whenever it turns from one slot to another, before that slot's
   events, and never dropped -- so no other event had to change. Every slot has a stable number for as long as
   the client sits there. The app keeps one state per slot: the active slot's is `AppState`'s own fields, as
   they always were, and another slot's is a `TableApp` kept aside and swapped in for its events and out again
   (`swap_slot`), so the two thousand lines that read those fields never learn there is more than one table.
   `switch_to` turns the window to another slot; `table_view_of` looks at one without turning; `slots` lists
   them with the turn marked (`turn_at`, from `YourTurn`). The lobby shows *Your tables* once there are two,
   the active one lit and *your turn* on the one that waits; a click is `LobbyAction::Focus`, which turns the
   app's state and tells the node `NodeCommand::Focus`, and the table window then shows that table. The node
   keeps the active slot until the window turns: a table founded or joined while seated takes its command in
   its new slot but does not become active on its own, and a slot that never gets its table -- a join refused
   -- goes a minute after it was opened once the window has turned elsewhere. The headless client needs none
   of this: its play is the node's own. Not done: one window per table (the felt shows the active table; the
   lobby's strip is where the player turns), and the turn's own pull of the window, which the owner can ask
   for once the strip has been seen.
4. **Measured.** On the bed, run C's scenario again (`tools/table-run.ps1 -Seats 3 -StartStack 200 -RehostAt 120 -Seconds 330`, `run081126-3`) on the `TableRun` build: the second table's first hand 15.7 s after the hosting (15.4 s in `run213600-3`), the joiners in its group 0.1 s and 5.1 s after asking, the tournament over at 149.2-152.8 s and every seat out of its group 10.1-11.1 s later, fifteen hands opened and fifteen finished on every seat, one genesis per hand per table, no certificate, 7.7 s per hand in the steady state. Stage 2: run C's scenario on the stage-2 build (`run082901-3`): 17 hands opened and 17 finished on every seat, one genesis per hand per table; the first tournament over at 98-102 s and every seat out of its group 10.3-11.6 s later; the second table's first hand 15.4 s after the hosting, both joiners in its group 0.1 s after asking; 10.8 s per hand in the steady state. **One client at two tables** (`tools/table-run.ps1 -Seats 3 -TwoTables -AlsoAt 60 -Seconds 300`: five
   nodes, n0 hosting A with n1 and n2, n3 hosting A-B with n4, and n1 asking to join A-B at 60 s without
   leaving A; the node's own autoplay acts at both): `run084503-3` -- n1 asked at 60.0 s, the node opened *slot 2
   of 4*, n1 was in B's group at 65.1 s and dealt B's first hand at 70.1 s; from then to the end it played
   both, 36 hands at A and 30 at B, 144 and 120 turns, 7.7 s and 7.6 s between hands -- a single table's
   pace at each -- with 59 hands opened across the two while both ran. `run083639-3`, the first attempt, is
   the S1-DQ row: the greeting into B's group tangled, B counted n1 out at 90.8 s, the second attempt at 120 s
   went through and the return road (D-031) took n1 back for B's hand #9; it played 21 hands there and 36 at
   A. `run085331-3`, the same scenario on the library with patch 0030: n1 in B's group at 65.1 s and dealt at 70.1 s, 37 hands at A and 31 at B (144 and 120 turns, 7.7 s and 7.5 s between hands, 61 hands across the two while both ran), no certificate; no greeting was heard twice in that run, so the patch's guard fired nowhere -- its proof is the tangle's mechanism read to the line and the whole-stack test through the patched library. **Stage 3:** `run091015-3`, the two-table scenario on the stage-3 build, the headless app routing every event by the node's markers: n1 asked to join B at 60 s, was in its group at 65.1 s and dealt at 70.1 s, and played 36 hands at A and 30 at B (144 and 120 turns, 7.7 s and 7.6 s between hands), no certificate, no panic. The lobby's strip itself is for the owner's eyes: two windows on one machine, one of them at both tables.

**Guard.** The library's tests unchanged (865), the bed's runs named in point 4, and the S1-DN row's tools.

**D-042 amended 2026-09-12 (S1-DX, the owner's rule): a client sits in no group it does not play at.** The
driver leaves a table's group in `close_table`, which every path that ends the table's play reaches (the
window's leave, a refused join, a founder that did not answer, the tournament's end ten seconds after the last
hand), at the driver's stop, on an invitation to the wrong group and on a failed join; the friendship may
linger (`FRIEND_LINGER`), the membership never does.

## D-044 — before the first hand, nobody waits for a seat that is gone

**Decided 2026-09-12, the owner's ruling** (*"nesmí tam být deadlock"*, for a seat that leaves, for one or
more that lose their line, heads-up and multiway alike).

1. **The word is the group's, by the line an invitation went over.** The library records, on both sides of
   an invitation, the friend number it travelled over; `patches/0033` reads it, so the founder knows the Tox
   key behind every member it invited from the moment it joins, and a joiner knows its founder's -- taught
   by nobody, so before the first hand. From it the driver keeps presence, silence and exits by Tox key
   beside the ones by application key that D-035, D-041 and S1-DT read after the hand.
2. **A seat is given back, on the two-second tick, when the group's word says it is gone**: it quit (at
   once -- the leaver's client says goodbye to the group), it timed out of the group, it has been silent in
   the group for `QUIET_LIMIT_S` (twenty seconds, S1-DT's clock, the felt's *offline*), or it never joined the
   group and its line is down `GROUP_JOIN_GRACE` (forty seconds) after sitting down -- a table that never got
   into its group lingers no friendship, so the others see the line drop within the library's friend
   timeout. Last, as before (S1-M), `SEAT_SILENCE_MS` (ninety seconds) of ping silence. The line names the
   reason: *seat N left the table before the first hand / timed out of the table's group / has been silent
   in the table's group for 20 s / never joined the table's group and its line is down / has answered nothing
   for 90 s -- and the seat is free again*.
3. **A joiner whose founder is gone leaves, with the reason on the felt and in the lobby**, on the same word
   about its founder, or when the founder said the roster again without this client
   (`Formation::released_before_the_first_hand`: named by the roster held until now and not by the next; a
   first list that does not name a joiner still joining says nothing, as before) -- **or on the founder's
   own answer to the lobby's question (D-040)**: an answer made after the table's advert that does not
   name the table is the founder's word that it offers it no more, seen within one asking (thirty
   seconds) whether or not the group ever held the founder -- the owner's case, a founder gone to the
   lobby with its client alive (S1-DX). Before this a joiner waited for ever. **Not once the table is set at
   this client (S1-EM):** the founder deals only once the table is set and its group holds everybody, and a
   table that dealt is answered without its advert too, so at a set table the founder's answer without it is
   the deal, not a leave -- the far seat's log (2026-09-12, 20:27 UTC) had the session at 46.7 s, the
   founder's hand #1 and its next answer at 47.4 s, and this rule sending the seat to the lobby at 48.0 s
   while its group join, a round trip behind the founder's, was still completing. A founder gone after the
   set is read by the rest of this point.
4. **Not the topic's unsubscribe.** It was built first and refuted on the bed: this client re-announces its
   topics by an unsubscribe and a subscribe a moment apart (`announce_topics`, on every tick while any lobby
   peer is off the table's topic), a tick between the two read as a leave, and a client killed mid-cycle left
   an unsubscribe as its last word; a three-second grace with the mesh's own view did not cure it
   (`run115253-3`, `run120811-3`). The transport that carries the hand says who left; the mesh does not.
5. **A table set to start goes on with the seats that remain, two at the least** -- **the owner's ruling,
   2026-09-12** (*"stůl může začít s nižším počtem hráčů, limit je samozřejmě heads-up"*), which amends the
   protocol: `PROTOCOL.md`'s `TABLE_READY` is legal once `PLAYER_LIST` named a roster of at least
   `min_players_to_start`, **or, after one that size was named, a roster the founder says again of at least
   two seats**. `Formation::started` remembers that a roster at the minimum was adopted here once;
   `Formation::floor` is then two, and it governs both the saying of a ratification (the gate in `adopt`)
   and the taking of one (`join::admit_ready`, which enforced the advert's minimum on every ratification
   received -- the register had read that check as never wired, and the first build of this point held a
   two-seat ratification on both sides until the test said so). And the driver is told the whole roster
   (`Seat::Roster`, from `seat_on_tox`), dropping the seats the formation no longer names: a joiner's driver
   had never been told a seat was gone and its group gate wanted it (`run130909-3`: the table set again at
   two at 44 s, the founder's first hand out at 52 s, the joiner's ninety seconds later at *2 wanted*). The
   kick on an unseating goes by the line the invitation went over (it had looked a Tox key up as an
   application key, and found nothing). A table never at its minimum stays short.
   So a Sit & Go that filled, lost a seat before the deal and got its roster said
   again deals to the seats that remain instead of waiting for a replacement -- the seat stays free in the
   lobby until the first hand, and a newcomer in that window makes the table whole again by the ordinary
   path. (Before the ruling the preset's *full and not before* held, and the section said so.)
6. **The bed's own traps, met on the way.** A headless client that left asked for its table again within a
   second and was seated again as the knob fired again (`run113830-2`: hand #1 dealt to a seat that was gone)
   -- now the `--join` name is spent by an own leave and `P2P_POKER_LEAVE_TABLE_AT` fires once; a kill at
   fifteen seconds landed after the deal (`run114821-2`, `run115037-2`: D-034's thirty-second timeouts, not
   this), so the kills are at eight; and twice the run directory taken from `ls -dt` was another day's.
7. **Measured.** Measured, the third round, on the group's word (`run122806-2`, `run122944-2`, `run123120-2`, `run123336-2`, `run123553-3`): a joiner that left at 12 s was given back at 16.3 s by its QUIT, two seconds after the leave, no hand dealt, the leaver in the lobby; a founder that left at 12 s, before the group had formed at its joiner, was read *never joined the table's group and its line is down* at 40.1 s and the joiner went to the lobby; a joiner killed at ~11 s, before it joined the group, was given back at 44.2 s by the same rule (the ping path alone had taken 94 s in `run120339-2`); a founder killed at ~12 s sent its joiner to the lobby at 40.1 s (it had waited for ever, and 90.2 s on the ping path in `run120555-2`); three seats with one killed at ~11 s: that seat given back at 44.2 s, the roster said again with two, the other joiner untouched to the end, no hand -- the preset starts when full, *waiting for players -- 2 of 3*. No false release in the round. The earlier rounds: `run113830-2` (the headless leaver re-seated within a second and hand #1 dealt to it), `run114305-2`, `run120024-2` and `run120202-2` (the unsubscribe path: a seat given back 4-6 s after a leave, a joiner leaving 3 s after its founder), `run115253-3` and `run120811-3` (its false releases at 4.1 s and 12.1 s).

**Guard.** `formation::tests::a_joiner_given_back_before_the_first_hand_knows_it_from_the_next_roster`,
`a_table_set_to_start_goes_on_with_the_seats_that_remain`, `a_table_never_set_does_not_start_below_its_minimum`,
the runs in point 7, the S1-DV row, `tools/build-tox.ps1`'s marker for `patches/0033`.

**Measured again after the ruling (point 5 built).** `run131918-3` (three seats, one killed at ~7 s, before it joined the group): the seat given back at 44.2 s, the roster said again with two, the table set again at 60.3 s, hand #1 dealt to seats [0, 1] at 65.2 s and begun at 68.5 s, twelve hands finished by 150 s at 6.7 s a hand, one genesis. `run130909-3`, before the driver was told the roster: set again at 44.3 s, the founder's hand #1 at 52.3 s, the joiner's ninety seconds later at *2 wanted*. `run131609-3`, the kill landing after the group had formed: hand #1 dealt to three at 22.2 s, the dead seat certified out on the clock at 53.4 s (D-034), sixteen hands to the two that remained at 6.7 s a hand -- the road after the deal, which stood already.

**Amended 2026-09-15, the owner's word (`S1-FN`)** -- *"na vzdáleném stroji se stůl samovolně uzavřel při reconnectu"*, *"připomínám, že nic nesmí stůl automaticky uzavírat než příkaz uživatele do GUI (myš atd.)"*, and on the fix proposed -- a question in the window instead of the leave -- *"vrať to zatím zpět: já myslím, že zjišťovat, že stůl byl gone při reconnectu, je nesmysl, když rozehraná hra se už nepropaguje ve veřejném lobby; pokud stůl už opravdu neexistuje (ostatní dohráli třeba), tak to už hodí chybu"*. **Point 3 holds only until the table is set at the joiner.** Once it is, nothing read about the founder sends the seat away: not its exit from the table's group, not its silence there, not its being outside the group with its line down after `GROUP_JOIN_GRACE`, not `SEAT_SILENCE_MS` without a ping answer (the lobby answer was not read after the set already, `S1-EM`). A game under way is not offered in the lobby, and the founder's line is read from this client's own copy of the group, which a reconnect can leave empty: the far seat's client, set at 13:58:56 and cut off from the Tox network for four seconds right after, read its founder that way 71 s after the set and left a table whose other seats were still waiting for it (they certified it out of hand #1 21 s later and played on). The founder's own roster said again without this seat (`Formation::released_before_the_first_hand`) still sends it back: that is the table's word, not a reading. A founder absent from a set table is then the hand's to handle like any other seat -- certified out at the opening after `S1-FM`'s allowance, or at heads-up the question its opponent is asked once it had been on the line -- and a player at a table that really is over leaves it from the window. `joiner_leaves_because` holds the rule, and `net::run::a_joiner_before_the_first_hand` guards it.

**Amended 2026-09-16, the owner's rule (`S1-FY`)** -- *"jediná událost, která ten stůl může zatím uzavřít, je, že to přikáže uživatel pomocí GUI"*, and *"ne že se zdraví peeři odpojí kvůli jiným peerům, kteří mají špatné spojení nebo dobrovolně opustili formující se stůl"*. **Point 3 holds for a client with no player (`--autoplay`) alone.** A window's joiner never leaves before the first hand either: it waits for a founder it cannot hear, with the reason on the felt, and asks again for a seat the founder gave back (two seconds after, then every thirty while the founder does not seat it; a refusal for good ends it); the founder's roster without it after the set is the table lost, said with the window kept. And **point 2 is not read through this client's own deafness**: at a table of three or more, a founder that hears no other seat gives back only a seat that quit the group, and a joiner that hears no other seat says its own line may be down instead of blaming its founder -- at a table of two the two readings cannot be told apart and nothing changes. A seat given back rejoins the group under a fresh member key, so the key dropped for good (`D-045`) never stands in its way. Measured: `run154347-3` and `run155205-3`, the S1-FY row.

**Amended 2026-09-16 again (`S1-GA`, `D-060`, `D-061`).** Point 2 has two more roads: a seat's own signed word that its player left gives the seat back at once, heard over the table's topic as well as its group (`S1-GA`); and the table's hearing gives back the seat the table cannot play with -- one that cannot hear a settled seat, or that two settled seats cannot hear, for `MESH_GRACE` (`D-060`). And a window's joiner whose founder is gone does not wait for it for ever: `FOUNDER_GONE_GRACE` after its reading it goes on at the table the lowest healthy seat founds again (`D-061`).

## D-045 — the table's word removes a member, and the founder's kick counts only with it

**Decided 2026-09-12, the owner's ruling** (*"žádný peer nesmí zůstat jako duch v tox skupině daného stolu,
pokud už nehraje; musí být odstraněn ostatními peery, co hrajou -- i kdyby to mělo znamenat úpravu tox core,
pro bezpečné kicknutí peera pomocí certifikací ostatních, aby ani founder ve 3+ hráčích nemohl libovolně
vyhazovat legitimní peery"*).

1. **The word.** Two things say a seat is out of the table's group: **the players' certificate** -- the table
   acted for the seat (D-036's majority, at D-034's clock) *and* the group has not heard from it for
   `QUIET_LIMIT_S` (twenty seconds), so it is a member that no longer plays and not a seat merely slow; and, before the first hand,
   **the roster the founder said again** without it (S1-M, D-044). The roster is fixed for the life of a
