   Carol*, *Carol is coming back*, *Carol is back* -- and the sentence under the steps says what the step under way
   waits on. A seat back before it was ever put out is done at once; *is back* stays four seconds.
2. **Two panels at most**, stacked at the top of the felt, and a count of the rest. This client's own way back is
   the only panel while it is under way: a client that cannot reach the table has nothing reliable to say about
   the others.
3. **From the node's facts**: `NodeEvent::TimeoutVotes` and `ReturnVotes` (the tallies the hand engine already kept
   for its log, now also a structured `take_return_tally`), `SitInAsked { seat }` (for every seat, where `D-057`
   had only this client's own), with `SeatLink`, `SeatCertified` and `HandBegan` the window already had.

**Guard.** `app::tests::the_wait_on_a_seat_is_shown_step_by_step_until_it_is_back` (the members' side of the far
founder's outage in `fe181646-3`, from its silence to dealt in again). `--table-preview --preview-waits` and
`--preview-waits-back` draw it.

**D-058 amended 2026-09-14 (the owner's word, four times: said while the table is not being played, never over a
hand that is -- said every time, and until the next hand is dealt).** First *"malé škobrtnutí: ta hláška Waiting for
tam nemá být, pokud už hraje zbytek hráčů po vyhození mrtvého peera atd."* -- with a screenshot of *Waiting for* a seat
that had left the table, every step to its certificate done and *Back on the line* turning, over a table that had dealt
on without it: the panel had no end but a return. Then, on `8f6555f`, which still said a certified seat over the felt
for four seconds and a returning one in a panel of its own: *"i ta coming back hláška nesmí vizuálně rušit aktuálně
živou a rozehranou handu"*. Then, on `4c33836`, which said the certificate in the table's log alone: *"zas ta hláška o
certifikaci hned zmizela dříve, než se začala hrát nová handa po vyhozeném hráči (stůl vypadal pro uživatele jako
zmrzlý)"* -- and for `D-057`: *"hláška Back in the game musí zmizet, jakmile dostanu hole cards po reconnectu"*. Then, on
`62e08af`, with a screenshot of the panel over a hand whose flop could not open without a seat that had left: *"ta hláška
Waiting for se neobjevuje spolehlivě pokaždé, když se řeší zastavení stolu kvůli neodpovídajícímu peeru, a také by bylo
dobré, aby ta hláška zůstala zobrazena až do úspěšného rozdání nové handy"*.

4. **While the hand stands on a seat, a panel says so**: the seat holds the turn (one no certificate has acted on
   yet) while it is off the line or the votes about it run; or a cryptographic stage -- the hand's opening before the
   deal, the deck, a reveal, the showdown -- by the node's word once the stage has stood on it for
   `STAGE_STANDS_AFTER_MS` (five seconds; `NodeEvent::StageStands`, from the stall tick, on change, before the deal as
   after it, for a seat the group still hears as for one gone from the line), and before the deal at once by the
   hand's own word (`HandWaiting`) when the seat is off the line. At its turn: its clock, the other seats agreeing to
   act for it (with the count), certified out as the table checks or folds for it. At a stage: *the cards cannot move
   on without it*, the other seats agreeing to end the hand (with the count), the next hand dealt without it. A seat
   off the line while the others still play is shown by its seat's link alone, and `S1-EI`'s older sentences follow
   the same rule.
5. **Certified out, the table goes on without the seat and says so until it is played again**: *The table goes on
   without Carol* -- certified out of hand #N, that hand finishing without it, the next hand dealt without it -- from
   the certificate until the turn is at a seat on the line in the same hand, or the next hand's cards are out; a hand
   called off after the certificate says it again until then. `SeatCertified` names its hand, and the node says it
   before it says the hand is over (`remove_by_the_word!` at the head of `hand_may_have_ended!`): a certificate this
   client's own vote completed at the stall tick had been said at the next tick, two seconds after `HandEnded`, and
   the window, holding no live hand by then, let the panel go. The table's log says *Carol is certified out of this
   hand; the table plays on without it*.
6. **Its way back is said at its seat and in the table's log, never over the felt**: *coming back* where *sitting
   out* stood, from its sit-in or the votes on its return until it is dealt in again; *Carol asks to sit in after
   hand #20* once per boundary, and *Carol is back in the game* under the header of the hand that deals it in. A return
   that goes quiet is not said past the hand after the one it was last heard at.
7. **`D-057`: this client's own *Back in the game* goes the moment its hole cards are here**, and is not said at all
   over a hand it already holds cards in (a short outage inside a hand); between hands it stays its four seconds.
8. **Said every time.** The felt reads the waits before every frame (`AppState::table_view_of` runs `tick_waits`), not
   at the sweep alone: the sweep is thirty seconds apart, and while it was the only thing writing the entries a stall
   that began after one was said at the next, or never. Four ways the panel had failed to come: that; a stall at the
   next hand's opening, which this window held no hand for (a seat that dies between hands holds exactly that stage);
   a seat the group still hears whose client answers nothing (the stage's word now needs no link reading); and the
   certificate's word after the hand's end (point 5).

**Guard.** `app::tests::the_felt_says_the_wait_on_a_seat_only_while_nothing_is_played` (the turn, the certificate
until the turn is at a seat on the line, the stage, the hand called off until the next hand's cards, the return),
`app::tests::a_stall_is_said_the_moment_it_is_known_and_held_until_the_next_deal` (no hand begun, no sweep; a seat
heard; the certificate after the hand's end), `app::tests::no_wait_is_said_over_a_table_that_plays_on`, and the
rewritten end of `app::tests::the_way_back_is_shown_step_by_step_until_dealt_in_again`; `--table-preview` with
`--preview-waits`, `--preview-waits-gap` and `--preview-waits-back`. Not measured on the bed: the panel is not drawable
there, and the four failures were read off the code against the owner's screenshot.

## D-059 — every wait for a seat shortens the next one at a cryptographic step

**Decided 2026-09-15, the owner's ruling** (*"chtěl bych vylepšit systém certifikací pro peera se špatným spojením,
taky pravidlem 3x a dost, tzn. že pokaždé, kdy bude celý stůl nucen čekat na peera, tak při každém zastavení hry
(každém čekání) mu odebrat 10 sekund času potřebného k certifikaci peera ven (je to i proti zneužívání rogue peerem,
který by si prodlužoval čas na přemýšlení nebo zdržoval hru)"*; asked whether a turn's time is cut as well, the owner
chose *only the cryptographic steps*; shown the measurement in point 1, *count from ten seconds, and never less than
ten*).

1. **A wait** is a cryptographic stage -- the hand's opening, the deck, the shuffle, a deal, a reveal, the showdown --
   that has stood on a seat for `WAIT_FROM_MS` = 10 000, or the seat's turn run past its deadline (the decision's time,
   the network's share and any reserve: the moment the other seats vote). Ten seconds is twice the slowest honest step
   measured: in the owner's games that day the far seat shuffled with its proof in 1 to 3 s, and in one game
   (`bc8304bd`) 4 shuffles of 22 took over five seconds, 5.3 s at the slowest -- the window's wait panel, which still
   appears at five, would have counted a slow machine. Each client counts on its own clock, once a stall, **when the
   stall is over** (`Hand::stall_now`, `hand::Waits`): the stage moved or the hand ended. Never this client's own seat;
   nothing at the table's first hand's opening while `S1-FM`'s minute for joining the table's group holds; nothing where
   no certificate could remove the seat (`D-036`'s floor); and **nothing for a stall during which this client heard none
   of the other seats of the table for `DEAF_AFTER_S` (14 s)** -- the group's members ping every twelve seconds, so a
   client that hears nobody for that long is the one cut off, and the library's own word on its line comes a minute
   late. The bed taught this one: in `run181556-3` the node whose line was cut counted the seat it could not hear.
2. **The cut** (`hand::patience_ms`): at a cryptographic step a client votes about the seat after the step's budget
   less `PATIENCE_CUT_MS` for every wait counted before, at most `MAX_PATIENCE_CUTS` of them, and never under
   `WAIT_FROM_MS`: at the table's thirty-second step 30 s, 20 s, and 10 s from then on (the third wait is counted and
   cuts nothing more there). A stall is counted when it is over, so it cuts only the steps after it. The carrier's
   reprieve for a seat whose traffic is still being delivered (`S1-BK`) is twice the seat's own time. **A turn is never
   cut** -- the owner's choice: the thirty seconds to decide and the three for the network are the player's (`D-034`),
   and a turn that runs out counts as a wait all the same.
3. **What it stops.** A client cannot stretch a turn past the network's share, but it could hold the deal back -- the
   shuffle, a deal, the reveal before its own turn, where no clock of its own runs -- and think for thirty seconds at
   every step. Now it gets that once, then twenty seconds, then ten, and every stall of ten counts again. A seat with a
   bad line costs the table the same way, less each time, and `D-032`'s three returns still bound how often it comes
   back.
4. **Local, the wire unchanged.** A vote still names the stage's own `deadline_ms`; a receiver checks that value and
   nothing about when the vote was cast, and a certificate needs a vote from every seat of `V(S)`, so the table votes a
   seat out when the most patient voter's clock says so. A client on an older build waits the whole budget, and a
   client back from a restart counts from nothing, so every seat should run the same build. The count is kept for the
   table for the whole tournament (`TableRun::patience`, cleared when the table is left); a return restores nothing.
   The bare abort (`may_abandon`, twice and three times the budget) is unchanged: the certificate still goes first.
5. **Said** in the client log (*seat 2 made the table wait (1 of 3): from now on this client waits 20 s for it at a
   cryptographic step before voting*), in the table's log (*Carol made the table wait (1 of 3): 20 s at a step from
   now on*), and in the wait panel's sentence (*It has made the table wait once: 20 s at a step from now on*).
   `PROTOCOL.md` says the shorter timer at `TIMEOUT_VOTE` and in §8.2.

**Measured on the bed** (`run181556-3`, `run183647-3`: three local seats, node n2's internet cut at the socket for 25 s
at 70 s and every 100 s after). The first build counted a wait the moment a stall passed ten seconds, and the cut node
counted the seat it could not hear -- *seat 1 made the table wait* at 81 s, eleven seconds into its own outage, and
again as its line came back; the certificate still needed the healthy node's vote, so nothing moved, but the word was
false -- which is point 1's counting when the stall is over and never through deafness. With that, the cut node
counted nothing through four outages. Both healthy nodes counted seat 2's first stall when it ended (100 s); its next
stall was voted about some twenty seconds into its stage (the vote at 120.3 s, the stall counted at the tick of
100.2 s) and certified unanimously; the ones after that ten seconds in (10.7 s and 11.7 s from the stage's
*waiting for seat 2*, on the two-second tick), and the fourth count said the least. Both healthy nodes held one genesis
on all 46 hands. The cut node came back each time by the return certificate (harness verdict BEHIND-REJOINED in both
runs), and twice in the second run opened a hand on its own view before the table's certificate reached it -- hand #8
re-derived at the certificate (`S1-BS`), hand #28 dropped for the table's copies (`D-038`) -- the roads a node back
from an outage takes, which the harness reports as *2 of 39 on a different genesis* for that node.

**Guard.** `table::hand::tests::the_table_waits_less_at_a_step_for_a_seat_that_made_it_wait`,
`a_wait_is_counted_once_when_the_stall_is_over`, `a_stall_this_client_was_deaf_through_counts_nothing`,
`a_turn_run_out_is_a_wait_and_its_time_is_never_cut`,
`no_wait_counts_while_the_first_hand_waits_for_its_seats_or_where_nobody_could_be_voted_out`;
`app::tests::a_seat_that_made_the_table_wait_is_said_with_its_time_at_a_step`.

**Amended 2026-09-16 (`S1-GK`).** A seat whose player left a set table by its own signed word, and whose client is out of the table's group, is voted about at once at every step and every turn -- the one wait this decision's clocks leave to nobody's patience. A certificate still needs every voter, and a voter that did not hear the word votes at the deadline; a seat back in the group has its clock again. Measured before: two players leaving the moment a table of ten was set (`churn182836-10`) were certified out of hand #1 only when their turn's clock ran out, 153 s after their words.

## D-060 — a table starts full of seats that hear each other

**Decided 2026-09-16, the owner's goal** (*"hlavním cílem, a taky kryptograficky (aby rogue peer nemohl škodit a podvádět),
během formování a usazování stolu, je odfiltrovat nezdravé peery (nespolehlivý internet) bez zamrznutí algoritmu, a pak
spustit už zaplněný plný stůl se zdravými peery"*, and *"na problémové peery nečekat moc dlouho, co nejmíň to jde, to odvoď
z měření"*).

1. **A seat says it is ready only when it hears every seat.** `TABLE_READY` (§4.3) was made the moment a roster was
   adopted, and `PROTOCOL.md`'s condition beside it -- *an established connection to every other listed seat* -- was
   read by nothing. So a table set with seats whose line was down or whose client was gone, and its first hand waited
   for them: ten seats over two machines with lines cut, clients killed and players leaving and coming back
   (`churn161800-10`) set at 85.9 s with a seat offline, and hand #1 took until 231.7 s to finish; four seats
   (`churn160721-4`) set with a dead seat and an offline one, and dealt their first hand to two. Now the node holds its
   seat's ratification (`Formation::hold_ratification`) and makes it on its two-second tick once every other seat of the
   roster is in its copy of the table's group and was heard there within `QUIET_LIMIT_S` (`seats_unheard`,
   `Formation::ratify_now`); a seat back at a table already set is not held. The table is set when the last seat has --
   and at that moment every seat heard every seat. The owner's earlier ruling stands for what happens after the set
   (`D-044` point 5).
2. **A seat says whom it cannot hear** -- `TABLE_HEARING` (`PROTOCOL.md` §7.11), signed by its application key, over the
   group and the topic, whenever that changes and every 6 s -- because the founder alone cannot see whether two joiners
   hear each other. A receiver takes one a second from a carrier and does not charge it to the chat's budget.
3. **The founder reads the table's hearing** and gives back the seat the table cannot play with, beside its own readings
   (`D-044` point 2). A seat still inside `GROUP_JOIN_GRACE` of sitting down is neither judged nor held against another.
   A settled seat is in trouble when it cannot hear a settled seat -- its own word, which costs a liar only its own seat
   -- or when at least two settled seats cannot hear it, so no single seat can have another given back. A trouble that
   lasts `MESH_GRACE` (20 s) gives the seat back: of several, a seat that no longer speaks first, then the most
   troubled, and between equals the later seated. Once every seat hears every seat, a seat that has not ratified for
   `READY_GRACE` (15 s) holds the table up and goes too. A seat that speaks of an older roster is sent the roster again,
   at most every 10 s. **A founder that is deaf judges nobody** (`S1-GE`): while every seat in its group has been silent
   for `DEAF_QUIET_S` (8 s) the fault is most likely its own line, and it gives back only a seat that said goodbye; and a
   seat whose own `TABLE_HEARING` came within `HEARING_FRESH` (15 s) is alive, so the founder's silence readings never
   give it back -- whether the table can play with it is the table's hearing to judge.
4. **A rogue seat.** It cannot stop the table starting: silent, it is given back by the founder's own reading; claiming
   it cannot hear others, it is given back on its own word; heard by all and never ready, it is given back at
   `READY_GRACE`. It cannot have a healthy seat given back: its word against another counts only beside a second
   seat's. It cannot forge another seat's word -- every word is signed by a key the roster names -- nor replay an old one
   into a new roster, which carries its serial.
5. **Measured**, the same plan both times (`-Seats 10 -There 3 -Seed 1601`: three lines cut, two clients killed and
   started again, two players leaving and coming back, all before 180 s, over this machine and the far one). Before:
   `churn161800-10` above. After (`churn163737-10`): the table set at 181.6 s, 1.6 s after the last fault, with ten seats
   of ten at one session everywhere; hand #1 dealt to all ten and over at 211.7 s. The founder gave back the seat whose
   player left 1.6 s after the word (`S1-GA`), a killed client's seat after 20.9 s, a cut line's after 21.9 s, and a seat
   that never came into the group 34.8 s after its line went.
6. **The owner's second phase, measured** -- faults the moment a table of ten is set, before its first hand is played
   (the owner: *"taky to otestuj pro jistotu"*). No run froze, split or closed a healthy seat's window. The founder's
   line and another seat's cut for 45 s at the set (`churn193159-10`): hand #1 waited for them inside `S1-FM`'s
   allowance and went on with all ten once they were back. The founder and another seat killed at the set
   (`churn194520-10`): the eight went on at one genesis a hand, the two certified out of the hand at 176 s. Two players
   leaving at the set: `S1-GK`, `S1-GL`, `S1-GN` and `S1-GO`, each found there -- after them both were certified out of
   hand #1 12 s after their words (`churn200256-10`), where it had taken 153 s. Between faults, a live member of the
   table's group was never silent there longer than 8 s while the table formed (38 silences over seven runs) nor 9 s
   while it played -- so `QUIET_LIMIT_S`, the twenty seconds after which a silent seat is given back, holds more than
   twice the longest silence of a healthy seat, and is where the wait on a dead one comes from.

## D-061 — a forming table goes on without its founder

**Decided 2026-09-16, the owner's wish** (*"i když se odpojí zakladatel stolu, kde už jsou připojeni jiní peeři, chtěl bych,
pokud to jde, systém umět kryptograficky bezpečně převést zakladatele na jiného zdravého peera"*, and among the faults a
forming table must ride, *"včetně poruch na straně zakladatele"*).

1. **The founder's authority before the set is the table key, and nobody else holds it** (§4.1, §4.3). Handing the key
   over needs its holder, and escrowing it among the seats -- shared out so a majority could rebuild it -- leaves a
   key two parties hold at once: a founder only partitioned would sign one roster while its successor signed another,
   and no seat could tell which is the table. So the table is not handed over: **it is founded again**, same name and
   same parameters, by one of its seats under a key of its own, and the seats go on there. Nothing of the game depends
   on who founded a table -- the cards, the chips and every hand are the seats' (§4.1: the founder's special position
   ends at `TABLE_READY`).
2. **When.** Before the set, a window's seat goes on when its founder said it left (`S1-GA`'s word, at once) or when it
   has read the founder as gone -- `D-044`'s readings, never through its own deafness (`S1-FY`) -- for
   `FOUNDER_GONE_GRACE` (20 s) past them -- and only while it knows the table still forms: nothing of a hand dealt
   there has reached it over the table's group, and either its founder admitted it (`JOIN_ACCEPT`, which a founder
   gives a stranger only before its table deals) or another seat is heard forming the table -- its `TABLE_HEARING`
   (§7.11), which a set table's seats never say, since the founder went or within `HEARING_FRESH` (15 s) before
   (`S1-GG`, `S1-GI`). A client that holds a roster without its session -- a player back at a table that has dealt,
   answered with the roster and not admitted -- so never goes on; a seat its founder admitted goes on even alone,
   and the players still arriving fill the table at its continuation. A client with no player (`--autoplay`) leaves
   as before.
3. **At whose table.** The lowest seat of the roster, the founder's excepted and seats passed over excepted, itself
   included.
   That seat founds the new table and says so with `TABLE_CONTINUES` (`PROTOCOL.md` §7.12): signed by its seat's key,
   carrying the new table's signed advert, whose founder must be the speaker. Every seat goes on at the lowest seat's
   word it has once that seat is its choice or lower, and passes over a choice that says nothing for `CONTINUES_WAIT`
   (20 s) -- 8 s when it does not hear that seat, which may still be founding, heard by others, since two seats must not
   both found one. A seat goes on by asking for a seat at the new table from what its player joined with -- the window's slot
   and window follow (`S1-FY`'s road). A founder that hears few of its seats and has a continuation's word goes on
   there too, as a seat.
4. **What a rogue can do.** It cannot move seats away from a founder they hear: a seat goes on only on its own reading.
   It cannot offer a table it did not found, nor speak for another seat, nor carry the word to another table, nor change
   the game: the continuation is founded from the old table's advert, and a seat hears the word only for a table of the
   same `table_params_hash`, name and password rule as the one it joined (`S1-GH`). As the lowest healthy seat it gains
   a founder's authority over the new table before the set -- who sits down -- and nothing over any hand; seats that do
   not want it leave. At a set table its word moves nobody: a set table's seats take no
   continuation word, and a client there without the session goes on only on its own reading of the founder and
   another seat's word that the table forms -- a rogue holding two seats could move that one client to a table of its
   own; no hand of the set table is touched.
5. **Measured** (`churn174703-6`: six seats over this machine and the far one, players arriving over 150 s, the
   founder's line cut from 50 to 130 s, one client killed at 128 s and started again at 165 s). The founder's line went
   at 52.6 s; two seats read it silent at 73.3 s and 75.6 s, and at 95.6 s seat 1 founded the continuation. The far
   seat 2 heard the word at 96.5 s and was seated there at 99.4 s; the old founder -- its lobby link up, its line to
   the group down -- heard it at 97.6 s and sat down there as seat 3 at 100.9 s; a player arriving at 98 s sat at the
   continuation at once. A far seat that had never reached the old table's group waited for its founder from 105.3 s
   (`GROUP_JOIN_GRACE` after sitting down) and went on at 125.4 s; the killed client, back, sat down at 169.0 s. The
   table set at 183.4 s with all six seats at one session, 3.0 s after the last seat reached the group, and dealt 21
   hands. Before `S1-GG`, `churn172308-6` founded a continuation of a table in play (above); nothing of that game moved.
   At ten seats (`churn195158-10`: the founder's line cut from 70 to 150 s, a client killed and started again, a player
   leaving and coming back, lines cut, all before 200 s): seat 1 founded the continuation at 113.3 s, 42 s after the
   cut, its seats went on from 117.3 s, the old founder sat down there as seat 9 once its line was back, and the table
   set at 219.9 s with all ten at one session, 20 s after the last fault, and dealt its hands. The founder's player
   leaving (`churn190530-10`, after `S1-GI` and `S1-GM`): the word at 63.5 s, the continuation founded by seat 1 at
   64.2 s, and all nine remaining players at it -- a table of ten that waits for a tenth, as it starts only full.

**Amended 2026-09-17 (`D-062`).** Point 3's last sentence -- a founder that hears few of its seats and holds a
continuation's word goes on there -- is withdrawn: the owner's founder followed a stale word to a withdrawn table
(`S1-GT`). A founder, a seat whose founder is gone, and a seat asking for a table of its game read the lobby first,
and the word serves the first seconds only; and a seat reads its founder gone by the group only through a line of its
own that is up, and not while the founder answers the lobby (`S1-GS`).

**Amended 2026-09-18 (`S1-HZ`, `S1-IA`).** *Not while the founder answers the lobby* means an answer that came after
the group last heard the founder, from a founder this client is still connected to; an answer from before the silence
counts for one gap between two askings and no longer. And the word goes to the old table's group as well as its
topic: the seat that founds keeps the old group for the minute it says the word, then leaves it. Measured with the
founder killed at 60 s before the set (four seats, `-PlayFaults '0:crash@60+500'`, seed 49): before, the seat that
had no poker peer on the lobby's line missed the word, founded a second continuation, and the two met through the
lobby at 145.0 s (`churn155115-4`; 203.0 s on the build before `S1-HZ`, `churn154146-4`); after, it read *seat 1
founded this table's continuation, said in the table's group* two seconds after seat 1 founded it (104.5 s) and sat
there at 109.1 s -- the table whole again 49 s after the kill (`churn161345-4`).

## D-062 — the seats of a forming table that lost its founder meet again through the lobby

**Decided 2026-09-17, the owner's wish** (*"peeři, kteří přišli o zakladatele stolu v době, kdy byli spolu na stole, se
předčasně rozštěpí na samostatné stoly ... a zůstávají na stolech osamoceni. Cílem je, aby se znovu navzájem sešli
prioritně na jednom stole, ale stále to vyřeš s vhodně nastaveným limitem, aby systém byl odolný proti nespolehlivému
internetu"*), on the owner's own three clients of 2026-09-16 20:32-20:38 UTC (`S1-GS`, `S1-GT`, `S1-GU`).

1. **Why a word alone splits a table.** `D-061` moved seats by one seat's word, `TABLE_CONTINUES`, said over the old
   table's topic for a minute; a seat that missed the word, or read its founder gone through its own line, founded a
   continuation of its own and sat there alone; and the founder followed any word it held. Three players sat at three
   tables. The word carries nothing a seat can weigh -- how many seats are at the table it names, whether that table is
   still offered -- and reaches only the seats the topic's mesh reaches at that minute.
2. **The origin.** Every seat keeps the table it first sat at -- its *origin*: the table's id, its founder's key, every
   application key its rosters seated with its seat, and the advert it was joined under (the game, the name, the gate).
   A continuation keeps the origin of the table it continues; the player's own leave forgets it, and so does a join to a
   table that is none of the origin's.
3. **The tables of one game**, read against the origin: the origin itself, offered by its founder; and every table
   founded by a key of the origin's rosters that plays the origin's game -- the same `table_params_hash`, name and
   password rule (`S1-GH`). A stranger's table of the same name is none of them; nor is another table of the origin's
   own founder. Each has a *rank*: the origin is 0, a continuation is the seat its founder held at the origin.
4. **Where the seats meet**: at the table of the game with the **most players** (the advert's count, which its founder
   re-says every 30 s); among equals at the origin, then at the lowest seat's. Only tables the lobby offers now -- heard
   within `OFFER_FRESH_MS` (90 s, three of the lobby's askings, `D-040`), joinable, not full, and not one that refused
   this client within `AVOID_FOR` (5 min).
5. **Who moves, and when**, every `RECONVENE_EVERY` (30 s):
   - a seat of a forming table whose founder is gone (`D-061`'s reading) goes to the best table offered, before it
     follows any word or founds anything; a table with a single player is taken only from a higher seat, since the
     lower seat's own table would rank above it. The word and `D-061`'s election serve the first seconds, before the
     lobby's asking has carried any advert;
   - the founder of a forming table goes on, as a seat, to a table of its game with more players than its own roster
     holds -- never on a word alone (`S1-GT`); its seats read its leave (point 7) and go the same way;
   - a seat asking for a table of its game (`S1-FY`'s asking again) asks for the best table offered instead when that
     is another; and when none is offered for `LOOK_LIMIT` (60 s), founds the game's continuation itself, from its
     origin (`S1-GU`);
   - a seat at a forming table whose founder it hears moves at nobody's word but its founder's: the founder decides for
     its table (`D-061` point 4 stands).
6. **A seat's own line is not its founder's absence** (`S1-GS`). Before the set, a seat reads its founder gone by the
   group only while its own Tox connection is up and has been for `QUIET_LIMIT_S`; and not at all while the founder
   answers the lobby's question (`D-040`) naming the table within `FOUNDER_ANSWER_FRESH_MS` (75 s) -- a founder alive
   with the group's line in trouble -- unless the founder has been out of the group's hearing for `FOUNDER_TOX_DEAD_S`
   (120 s), past which the table cannot form and the seats go on. The founder's own signed word (`S1-GA`) stands
   whatever the line says (`S1-GM`).
7. **The founder's word reaches every seat.** The founder's `TABLE_LEAVE` goes to every seat of its roster over the
   join channel too (§7.10, the mirror of `S1-GP`): a seat not yet in the group, at a founder its topic's mesh did not
   reach, learned its founder gone from the lobby's asking half a minute later and went on twenty seconds after that.
8. **What a rogue can do.** Nothing about the cards, the chips or any hand: a table of the game is founded from the
   origin's advert and plays its game. It can found a continuation and say more players sit there than do (the advert's
   count is its founder's word): seats that read the lobby go there, find its real roster, and read the lobby again --
   a table that refuses them is avoided for five minutes, and a table with fewer seats than another of the game loses
   them at the next reading. It cannot move a seat that hears its founder, cannot offer a table it did not found, and
   cannot carry the word to another table.
9. **Limits.** A seat alone at its own continuation with no other table offered for a minute founds nothing new (it
   already has a table) and waits for players from the lobby; two continuations of equal count and the same rank
   cannot exist. Oscillation is bounded by the reading's pace (30 s), the advert's freshness and `S1-GR`'s wait for a
   key that keeps sitting down and leaving.
10. **Measured**, 2026-09-17, over this machine and the far one (`tools/table-run-churn.ps1`, its new `-FarNodes` and
    `-PlayFaults node:kind@at[+for]` -- a line cut, a client killed and started again, a player leaving and asking
    again -- at any second of the run):
    - `churn135802-5` (five seats, two far; a player leaving at 75 s and coming back, a far seat's line cut 81-116 s,
      the founder's player leaving at 101.6 s with four seats forming): the founder's word reached every seat directly
      within 0.1 s (point 7); seat 1 founded the continuation 0.7 s after it; the two other seats went there through
      the lobby 1.7 s after the word, the far one with its line to the group cut at the time; the returning player
      joined the continuation by its name 12 s later; four of four remaining players at one table.
    - `churn153242-5` (five seats, two far; a far player leaving at 72 s and coming back at 220 s, the founder's
      player leaving at 121.9 s with three seats forming): the word reached two seats directly within a second and
      the third -- a seat that had sat down 30 s before, its join connection gone -- not at all; that seat was the
      lowest and founded nothing, the next founded the continuation 24 s after the word (`D-061`'s 8 s and 20 s
      waits), the one seat with the word went there 7 s later, the third through the lobby 20 s after its own
      reading of the founder, and the returning player 17 s after coming back: four of four at one table.
    - `churn131041-5` (the shape of the first, before `S1-GY`): the word within 0.1 s, the continuation 0.1 s later,
      two seats there within 2 s -- and at 59.5 s the continuation's founder went back to the old table on its stale
      advert, the two seats followed, the three asked for tables since gone for a minute and a half, and all four
      met at a fresh continuation only at 160 s.
    - `churn134150-3` and `churn152505-4` (the founder's player leaving a SET table by word, three and four seats):
      certified out by the rest 8 s and 3 s later with its word, the game on heads-up, 30 and 37 hands at one genesis.
    - `churn140638-6` (six seats forming, a far seat's own line cut 103-173 s): the cut seat read its own line
      (`S1-GS`), founded nothing, was given back at 145.7 s and the table set with five 1.7 s later; its client then
      asked every 30 s for a table that had started, refused as *advert expired* each time (`S1-HB`).
    - `churn130206-6` and `churn131817-10` (the founder's line cut for 60-80 s while six and ten seats formed, before
      `S1-GX`): the founder gave four and seven seats back while its own line was cut; the seats asked again and were

      founded -- the seats read the founder alive by its lobby answers (point 6) and waited.
    - `churn150139-10` (ten seats, four lines cut 150-210 s while the table formed, before `S1-HE`): the table set in
      two halves at 229.6 s -- four seats on the roster the founder had ratified and then changed, the founder and
      five others on the next one, no hand at the founder to the end.
    - `churn150939-10` (ten seats, five lines cut 150-210 s while the table formed): set at 269 s with all ten, nine

    - With every fix of the day built (`churn162104-6`, six seats forming, a far seat's own line cut 105-175 s): the
      cut seat read its own line and founded nothing, was given back at 183.6 s, the table set 1.4 s later with five
      and dealt 23 hands; the cut seat's client asked twice, was answered *advert expired* twice, and stopped: *the
      table started without this seat* (`S1-HB`). `churn162945-10` (ten seats, two far, the founder's line cut 71.6-151.6 s while the table formed, a
      client killed and back, lines cut, a player leaving and back, all before 200 s; `S1-GX` and `S1-HE` built): the
      founder gave back one seat 56 s into its own cut -- by the never-joined road, which had no own-line guard and
      has one now -- and none by the hearing's judgement; the seat was back 4 s later; a seat whose player left by
      word was freed at once by the word; the table set at 203.2 s, 3 s after the churn's end (238.5 s before
      `S1-GX`), with nine -- a far seat that could not hear three seats given back 1.3 s before the founder's

## D-063 — a player's own signed leave counts against no floor

**Decided 2026-09-17, the owner's rule** (*"obecně nesmí dojít, při všech možných situacích na nespolehlivém internetu
během poker hry, na stole k deadlocku ... dobrovolný odchod peerů"*), from `S1-GW`.

1. **The floor is for the silent.** `D-036`'s floor -- two voters at least, more voters than seats named -- keeps a group
   short of a majority from certifying the rest out, since the rest may be playing on at the other side of a partition.
   A player that left by its own signed word (`TABLE_LEAVE`, §7.10) is at no other side: it is at no table. Its word is
   its consent, and asking a majority for it left two of three leaving a table with a third that could only wait.
2. **The certificate carries the word.** `TIMEOUT_CERT` gains `n(2) resignations`: the signed `TABLE_LEAVE` of every
   seat it names whose player left, which every receiver checks as it checks the votes -- the seat's own key, this table,
   the reason. The votes stay as they were: every voter votes about every seat named, at once for a seat gone by its word
   (`S1-GK`). Against the floor only the seats named without a word count: with `Q` those, a certificate is legal when
   `|V(S)| >= 1` and either `Q` is empty or `|V(S)| >= 2` and `|V(S)| > |Q|`. A seat named with its word is out of the
   table for good (`D-047`'s road), not absent: nobody returns from a leave.
3. **What it does not change.** Heads-up (`D-007`: nothing at two seats; the leave word ends the game at the window,
   `S1-FQ`); a seat that fell silent without a word, which the floor guards as before; the vote, the digest, the
   collective stage. A word that is not the seat's own -- another key's, another table's -- is no resignation, and a
   certificate carrying one is refused. A seat that left before the set holds no seat at the set table, so no old word
   can name it (`S1-GA`).
4. **Measured**, 2026-09-17 (`tools/table-run-churn.ps1 -PlayFaults`, over both machines):
   - `churn141515-4` (four seats, two players leaving by their signed word at 121 and 126 s in hand #7): in hand #8 the
     two that stayed certified both out together with their words 2.4 s after the hand opened -- two voters naming
     two, which the floor forbade -- and played heads-up on, 20 hands. Hand #7 ran to its budget (63 s): one of the
     two had acted at the stage before leaving and was a voter the round could not close without (`S1-HA`).
   - `churn143804-10` (ten seats, three far; a line cut at 151 s, a client killed at 160 s and back at 205 s with its
     record, a player leaving by word at 173 s, all in hand #3): one certificate at 264 s named five seats -- the two
     faulted, the leaver with its word, and the two far seats the carrier had lost -- with five voters against four
     quiet; the returned client sat in again at hand #5, the far seats at hand #8, the cut one at hand #10; eleven
     hands, the three that had aborted hand #3 by their own deadline adrift for four hands and back by `D-038`.
   - The play phase over both machines, the same day: `churn125450-5` (five seats, a far seat's line cut 64-134 s in
     hand #1): certified out 61 s after the cut, back at the boundary of hand #4, 19 hands at one genesis.
     `churn134826-6` (six seats, the founder's line cut 121-181 s and a far seat's 128-173 s in hand #3): no deadlock;
     the certificate about the founder completed in hand #5 at 283 s, hands #3 and #4 having run to their budgets
     because the cut far seat was a voter (`S1-HA`); 24 hands, the founder back at hand #11. `churn145341-10` (ten
     seats, a second line cut 35 s into the certification of the first): the first certified 32 s after its cut, the
     second in the next hand 33 s after, both back by `D-032` at hands #7 and #9, ten hands at one genesis.
     `churn143026-10` (three lines cut at once in hand #2 of ten): the hand ran to its budget, the three were back,
     the next hand opened with all ten. `churn151819-3` (three seats: one cut and certified out in 32 s, then the
     other cut heads-up): the window's question 41 s after the second cut, withdrawn when the seat came back, the
     hand ended on its budget, both back in play by hand #18.
   - What the same bed showed of the carrier: `churn144601-10` (ten seats, the founder's line cut 151-197 s and
     another's 158-203 s in hand #3) crawled from stage 25 to 51 in 280 s -- the vote about the founder at 8/9, the
     ninth voter fetching two hundred missing messages from each of nine peers after every seat had re-said the whole
     hand to it (`S1-HD`), a betting stage bounded by nothing but the hand's 39 minutes; and `churn142248-10` (two
     lines cut 5 s apart at the set) held hand #1 for 268 s the same way. The carrier's asking for missing messages
     grows with the seats -- 0.06 a second at three, 0.24 at four, 0.68 at six, 1.3 at ten -- and ten seats with three
     relay-only seats on a four-core box is the transport's limit, not the protocol's; `S1-GZ`, `S1-HA` and `S1-HD`
     take the table's own traffic off it, and the ten-seat runs after them are in the rows.
   - With every fix of the day built, ten seats with TWO far seats: `churn154849-10` (no fault): set at 135 s, nine
     hands of 16-35 s at one genesis, the carrier still asking 1.2 times a second and the ratification echo still
     thirty copies a seat -- every crypto stage waits on most seats for a moment -- which the third cut of `S1-GZ`
     answers (a seat heard at no stage of the hand only). `churn155636-10` (two lines cut 5 s apart in hand #3):
     the hand ended at the stage's deadline (`S1-HA`), both seats came back inside hand #4 and one seat re-said it
     to them (`S1-HD`), five hands, no certificate needed. `churn160421-10` (a second line cut 35 s into the first's
     certification): the first certified 36 s after its cut, the second in the next hand 34 s after its own, both
     and a far seat the carrier had lost back at hand #10, eleven hands. `churn161222-10` (five of ten cut at once
     in hand #4): the hand ended at its deadline, the window asked *5 seats have been unreachable ... and the 5 on
     the line cannot certify them out (D-036): wait for them, or leave* (`S1-GV`), the five came back and the table
     played on -- with a local seat silent in the group for 101 s and hands of 90 s: the carrier at ten.
     With the third cut of `S1-GZ` (`churn164317-10`, no fault): set at 93 s, seventeen hands of 12-14 s at one genesis,
     two to six ratification copies answered a seat in the whole run, the carrier asking 0.9 a second.

## D-064 — the automatic search for a game

**Decided 2026-09-17, the owner's design** (*"kompletní, robustní systém automatického vyhledávání turnajů a
matchmakingu"*: one button, a format and a number of games at once, a modal window with the clock and the
estimate and the queue and the seats held and one cancel button; a backend that scores tables, expands the number
it looks at, lets a table it founded start short of full, manages more games than one, cancels without a leak; a
queue of its own beside the lobby, sliced the same way; dynamic timeouts; nothing that could freeze, leak or be made
to run code). Built in `src/net/matchmaker.rs` (the rules, with their tests), `src/net/run.rs` (the node's roads),
`src/app/mod.rs`, `src/gui/render.rs`, `src/main.rs` (`--search`), `PROTOCOL.md` §7.13, `NETWORK_STACK.md` §6.

1. **A reservation is a seat.** The search reserves by asking for a seat at a forming Sit & Go (`JOIN_REQUEST`),
   and holds it as any seat is held -- in the table's group, judged by its founder like any other. Nothing lighter
   exists in the protocol, and nothing lighter would let the table start the moment it is full. Each reservation
   is a slot of the node's own, marked the search's; the window draws no table window for it until it is a game
   (the owner: the system may close only windows it opened itself -- so it opens none until there is a game).
2. **Dynamic queue expansion.** A search holds seats at up to `DQE_START = 4` tables from the start and one more
   every step of waiting, up to a cap: heads-up and *any* every 30 s up to `DQE_MAX = 10`; six seats every 45 s up
   to 8; the full ring of ten every 60 s up to 6. Less aggressive for the bigger tables because every seat held is a group this
   client talks in, and a group's asking for missing messages grows with its seats (`D-063` point 4: 0.06 a second
   at three seats, 1.3 at ten).
3. **Capacity adaptation.** A table the search founds advertises `min_players_to_start = 2` under a name that
   begins `Auto Sit & Go`, and its founder says it is ready at its capacity -- the seats minus one for every
   `CAPACITY_STEP` (90 s) it has stood unfilled, never under two. The advert never changes: a founder that
   re-signed its parameters would make its own table unjoinable (`§7.2` rule 7); only the founder's own rule for
   when it says it is ready does. A joiner reads the same rule off the advert's name and the age at which it first
   saw the table.
4. **Arming: a joiner ratifies only what it is willing to start now.** The founder ratifies last (`S1-HE`), so a
   table cannot start without every seat's ratification, and a seat's ratification is therefore its consent to
   start. A search holding five reservations with one game wanted ratifies at most one of them at a time -- the one
   closest to starting, kept `COMMIT_TTL` (45 s) before another may be preferred -- so two tables cannot start under
   it in the same second and it never has to walk out of a game that began. A search founder holds nobody to
   `READY_GRACE` before it wants to start itself; a seat unarmed at another player's full table is given back by
   that founder's `READY_GRACE` as before, which is the right answer for a seat that would not play there.
5. **Seats flow to the lower key.** Two searchers who both founded would each join the other's table and two half
   tables would start together. So a client that founded joins another search table only when that founder's key
   is lower than its own, and a client founds only after `found_after` -- ten seconds, plus fifteen for every
   searcher of a compatible format whose key is lower (capped at four), plus ten when relayed -- so the lowest
   key founds first and the rest see its table inside a lobby round and join it. An *any* search founds the format
   most searchers want (six seats between equals, then heads-up, then the full ring) -- amended below: ten seats
   unless the others named a format.
6. **The queue.** A searching client says so on `/p2p-poker/search-queue/1` and on the slice its own key names at
   every depth, every `SEARCH_PRESENCE_EVERY_MS`, and once more when it stops (`SEARCH_PRESENCE`, §7.13): the
   lobby presence's mirror, judged the same way, sliced with the lobby. Every client counts the searchers; the
   window shows the count and their average wait; the search reads its founding order and an *any* search's
   format off it. It is never an input to any game decision.
7. **The goal, and the cleanup.** When as many games run as asked for -- tables the search started and tables the
   player sat down at by hand both count -- every other reservation is left by the player's own signed word
   (`TABLE_LEAVE`: free before the set, a resignation after it under `D-063`), the queue is told, and the window is
   told which slots are games now; more games started in one moment than asked for, the ones started last are
   left. A cancel does the same without the games, on the click: the modal is gone before the node answers, the
   node gives every seat back and says so, a step queued before the cancel does nothing.
8. **Every wait is bounded, and the bounds stretch with the network.** A join nobody answers is given up after
   `join_wait` (20 s, +15 relayed, +10 with fewer than three poker peers, at most 60); a founder unheard for
   `founder_patience` (45 s, 75 relayed) is left; a table that refused this client or answered nothing is avoided
   `AVOID_FIRST` (120 s), twice as long each time up to `AVOID_MAX` (600 s); an advert older than `OFFER_FRESH_MS`
   is not reserved at; the search ends after `SEARCH_MAX` (30 min) and says so. `D-062`'s roads are a played
   table's: a seat the search holds goes on nowhere, it is given back and another is taken.
9. **Security.** One new message, three small integers, signed, capped at `SEARCH_PRESENCE_MAX`, rate-limited per
   neighbour and per author, its two enumerations bounded, `Reject`ed when malformed, held in a bounded book. No
   new RPC and no new parser anywhere else: every seat the search takes and gives back travels the join RPC, the
   advert and the leave word this protocol already validates. The search's own state is a list of at most
   `DQE_MAX` reservations and a bounded map of avoided tables; every loop of its tick is over those and the
   lobby's bounded store. A request from the window is clamped, never refused.
10. **The window.** *Find a game* in the lobby opens the dialog -- format, games at once, *search again when the
    game ends* -- remembered in the profile with what past searches took. The modal: the spinner and the clock,
    the format, a bar of the fullest seat held against what its table needs, the estimate (the search's own once
    it holds a seat; before that, what searches of the format took before), the searchers and their average wait,
    the seats held with each table's fill and capacity, the games running against the games asked for, the phase,
    the network's one warning (the carrier's line down, nobody on the line, behind NAT without a relay), and one
    button, *CANCEL SEARCH*. Repainted four times a second while it is up.
11. **The owner's bonus, three ideas built.** *Search again when the game ends* (the request kept, the search
    restarted when a game it started is over -- `--search-again` on the bed). *What it took before*: the profile
    keeps the last twenty searches that found a game, by format, and the dialog and the window say the median
    until the search has a measurement of its own. *Relay-aware scoring*: a table whose founder is reached through
    a relay is read `RELAY_PENALTY_S` (20 s) further from starting -- a relayed founder is a slower group for
    every seat, and the relay's budget is spent by every seat at once.
12. **Measured**, 2026-09-17 (`tools/table-run-search.ps1`, read with `tools/fold-search.py`):
    - `search190453-4` (four *any* searchers on this machine, before `S1-HF`/`S1-HG`/`S1-HH`): two founded
      six-seat tables at 27 and 35 s (twenty seconds in, being relayed); one client took seats at both within a
      second of seeing them; the other two asked and were answered *Failed to dial the requested peer* at once
      (`S1-HF`), stood at no table for 45 s and founded their own. Joiners armed the fullest table one seat under its
      capacity at 208 s (three of six at a capacity of four), the founder armed its own when the capacity reached
      its three seats at 298 s, and the table set at 299.6 s -- 290 s after the searches began -- with three; the
      other three reservations were given back within a second, five hands were dealt at one genesis and a seat
      busted on its 300 chips. The fourth client stood alone at its own table to the end (`S1-HH`: four players
      wanted heads-up, not six seats). The queue's count reached three at every client within 40 s.
    - `search191717-6` (six searchers on this machine -- heads-up, six seats, any, any, six seats, heads-up -- one
      cancelling at 46 s and searching again at 66 s, one line cut 54-73 s; `S1-HF`/`S1-HG`/`S1-HH` built): an
      *any* client founded heads-up and the heads-up client took the seat: **set at 39.5 s, 28 s after both
      searches began**, three hands, the tournament over at 66 s. The cancel gave its one reservation back in the
      same second; the search again found a six-seat game. The six-seat searchers and the second *any* one met at

**Amended 2026-09-17 evening (the owner: *Automatic nejdřív zkusí 10 míst a podle stavu fronty určí rychlost
snižování; v prvních ~40 s nereagovat na falešnou nulu*; and the third format is the full ring of ten, not nine),
`S1-HK`.** Point 3's fixed 90 s step is gone: a search table's founder needs one seat fewer every
`capacity_step(waiting, missing)` -- 30 s when nobody waits in the queue, 180 s when as many wait as the table lacks,
in proportion between (the searchers already seated at the table do not count as waiting; they search on until the
game starts). Point 5's founding: an *any* search founds ten seats (`CUSTOM` with the rated numbers and a minimum of
two) unless the others named a format, and founds nothing while the queue is unknown -- until a presence is heard,
or the line has carried a poker peer for 40 s, or a minute has passed; an unknown queue reads as the slow step and
the window says *measuring*. Point 11: an *any* search forgives a table 10 s of estimate per seat above two, so a
ten-seat table 90 s from starting is preferred to a heads-up one 20 s away. What it costs: two players alone wait
about four minutes for their heads-up game at a ten-seat table (eight fast steps), four players about three; what it
buys: games of the size the crowd allows, and no heads-up tables founded on a silence that meant nothing.


**Amended 2026-09-17, late evening (`S1-HM`).** Point 4 is cut to the heads-up case: at a search table of more
than two seats a joiner ratifies from two seats whenever its search arms it, and the founder alone times the set --
it ratifies last, so nothing starts on a joiner's word. The joiner's estimate of the founder's capacity is only a
preference between tables now, never its condition to ratify. A founder's capacity is a floor from every reading:
it never rises again.

**Amended 2026-09-18 (`S1-HR`..`S1-HW`, the owner's second evening).** Point 5 reads: seats flow to the founder
that is not reached through a relay only, whatever the keys, and between equals to the lower key; a relayed client
founds thirty seconds later than a reachable one. A founder holds its own table while it sits at a bigger search
table it would yield to. A founder whose table gave three seats back before the set withdraws it, and each such
table doubles the wait before founding again; no founding for `found_after` after a seat was given back. A table's
avoidance strikes are remembered. The search window says what a founder waits for. The owner's standing
requirement, said the same night: **the system must not freeze in any phase -- searching, forming, starting, the
hands to the tournament's end -- and must resolve every situation of an unreliable network by itself: peers that
drop, peers that leave, packets that are lost, peers that lie.** Every rule of this decision is read against it.

**Amended 2026-09-18, at night -- the search seats as many players together as it can (`S1-IB` to `S1-IE`).**
The owner's word, after an evening of his own clients in which three *any* searchers ended as one heads-up game and
one player alone for ten minutes: *Find a game should try to find and found a table with as many players as it can*
-- and, repeated with it, the standing one: *the system must not freeze, and goes on resolving an unreliable network
by itself -- outages, peers leaving, rogue peers.* What had happened: the far founder's line dropped; its two seats
released it and sat down together at a table one of them founded; it came back, one of the two took a seat at its
table **as well**, consented at both, and the founder whose clock was older -- it had run at the fast step through
the whole outage, the queue reading empty to a client that could hear nobody -- set heads-up with it.
1. **One forming table holds a player.** A search sits at one search table of more than two seats for each game it
   wants. A player held at two is counted at both and fills neither; the rest of the expansion (point 2) stands for
   heads-up tables and for tables players made by hand.
2. **Seats go where more players sit.** The seat moves only to a table where strictly more players sit than at the one
   left -- so two seats never trade places -- once a minute, and never from a reachable founder's table to a relayed
   one's. A client that founded goes to another search table where more players sit than at its own, whoever's key is
   lower; between equals the key and the relay decide as in point 5, and a client reads itself behind a relay for the
   whole search once it has been, because its own reading flaps while every other client goes on seeing it relayed.
3. **Consent goes to one big table:** the most players, then the founder that can be reached, then the lower
   founder's key -- an order every client reads the same off the same tables. The founder's own table is ranked among
   them, which is `S1-HU` said once.
4. **The founder's clock is integrated, and stands while the founder is deaf** -- its table carrier's line down, or no
   poker client connected at all. One reading of a smaller queue moves it by that second, not to where the fast step
   would have had it from the start.
5. **No seat is asked for while this client's own line is down.** It could not be heard at the table, which would
   count it among its players all the same.
6. **No hold here outlasts its cause.** More players together is a preference and never a condition to wait on: a
   table that could have started two minutes ago by this client's own reading of its founder's clock keeps its seat and
   its consent and no longer holds the search to itself; the clock stands for the outage and still comes down to two;
   a founder unheard is left after the patience the search already keeps; nobody compatible in the queue, and a heads-up
   table starts as it did.
7. **The window shows the number that falls:** the rings of a held table are the players its founder needs now, the
   table's size beside them in words, *about* where the number is this client's reading of another founder's clock;
   *about to start* is said of a table with the players it needs, not of every table consented at; a seat alone with
   an empty queue has no estimate.
Measured: `search215457-3` (three local clients, the founder's line cut for 200 s: its capacity stood at six for the
152 s the cut was read, the table set with three at 452 s); `search220957-4` (the four-client plan of `S1-HM`: one
table, four players, set at 267 s, as before); `search213621-3` (the far founder first: a founder asking at the fuller
table, and the two holes points 4 and 5 close). Owed: the owner's live clients, for a founder dark on both lines.

## D-065 — a vote that does not come stops being a veto

**Decided 2026-09-18 on the project owner's ruling** (*"ano souhlasím"*, to the proposal that answered `S1-AQ`:
keep unanimity and make it reachable -- a vote is also a question, and a voter that does not vote loses its veto
for the hand and nothing else), under the owner's requirement of the same day (D-064's amendment): the system must
not freeze in any phase, and must resolve every situation of an unreliable network by itself. It is what D-026 asked
for in 2026-09-03's words -- *make the certificate reachable, not another way to stop*: a hand that hangs refunds
the staller as surely as one voided, and a voter that never votes was the accomplice that made it hang.

1. **The hole.** A certificate needs a vote from every seat of `V(S)`. One voter that said nothing -- gone,
   stalled, behind, or a client that plays every turn and never votes -- held every certificate about anybody
   else. At a cryptographic stage the hand ended on its deadline naming nobody and the next hand opened with the
   same seats, so one dead seat and one silent voter cost the table every hand after; at a betting stage nothing
   ends a stage (`past_deadline` is false there by construction) and it stood until `hand_deadline_ms` -- at a
   Sit & Go 29 min at four seats, 34 at five, 39 at six, 55 at ten; and seats that held different frames split
   their votes over who was late (`split182531-10`), so no set could complete. `S1-HA` had answered one shape --
   a voter gone from the group -- by giving the hand up at the deadline.
2. **A vote is also a question.** A `TIMEOUT_VOTE` says its voter accepted nothing from the seat at that stage,
   and a seat holding that frame now says it again under its author's signature (`Hand::vote_asks`,
   `run.rs` `answer_a_vote`): one answerer -- the lowest dealt-in seat that is not the one named, not gone from
   the group and not heard voting the same, `S1-HD`'s rule -- and the next when that one holds nothing; a vote
   about the receiver itself is answered with its own frames of the stage, and one naming it silent with its own
   votes and copies there and every frame of that stage it holds. Once per hand, stage, seat and cause. The client
   had re-sent only its own frames (the resend loop; `D-033`'s re-say to a seat back on the line).
3. **A voter silent about the round is voted about in turn** -- `TIMEOUT_VOTE` `cause = 2`,
   `CAUSE_SILENT_VOTER` (`PROTOCOL.md` §4.8): one stage budget after this client's last vote about the round's
   seats and after its own copy (`S1-BT`'s air), at once for a voter the node reads as gone from the table's group
   (`S1-HA`'s reading); only while the certificate naming the round's seats and that voter together clears
   D-036's floor; never about a seat the stage waits on. The vote starts the round's air again, so the second
   round has a budget before the local abort at a cryptographic stage, whose three-budget ceiling stands. A
   voter that votes and keeps its copy of the certificate back is a silent voter too: the certificate stage needs
   every voter's copy, and a betting stage's forced action waits on that stage.
4. **One certificate names the round's seats and the silent voters together** -- D-036's greatest sealable set,
   one subject per seat by this client's own view (quiet where the stage waits on it here, silent where it does
   not) -- unanimously among the rest, under both floors with the silent voters counted among the named; at least
   one seat named without the cause, and at a betting stage exactly one, the seat to act.
5. **What the table takes from a silent voter is its veto for the rest of the hand and nothing else**
   (`vetoless`): it leaves `V` of every later certificate of the hand; it is not struck, stays in `R(k+1)`, is
   not attributed by an abort resting on the certificate (`attributed` is the seats named without the cause), and
   no word is kept for its client. A seat merely slow loses nothing it needs; a seat really gone is named by the
   next hand's opening as any quiet seat is; a client that never votes can no longer hold a certificate about
   anybody.
6. **What this does not do.** The floor is unchanged: where the quiet seats and the silent voters together are
   half the live seats or more, no certificate forms and the table waits as D-036 says -- the window asks the
   player to wait or to leave (`D-066`, the same day, answers that case). A lying voter is still unprovable (Q-08), and one voter's word that another is
   silent seals nothing while the rest heard that voter. The heads-up rules (D-007) are untouched.
7. **Measured.**
   In the engine, tests first: `a_voter_that_never_votes_is_named_silent_and_the_round_closes_without_it` (five
   seats, one quiet, one that never votes: no seal inside the air, the silent vote one budget later, one
   certificate naming both among the three, the hand ends, the quiet seat out, the silent voter kept, one
   genesis on all four), `a_voter_gone_from_the_group_is_named_silent_at_once` (and the floor that fails when
   naming it would leave two voters for two seats), `one_voters_word_that_another_is_silent_names_nobody`,
   `a_voter_that_keeps_its_copy_back_is_named_silent`, `a_vote_reads_as_a_question` (which caught the question
   read under the payload's cap -- it answered nothing); `tests/timeout_certificate.rs`
   `a_betting_stage_is_not_held_by_a_voter_that_never_votes` (five seats played to a turn: the certificate
   names the seat to act and the silent voter, the table acts for the seat, the hand goes on, the seat to act
   leaves the roster and the silent voter keeps its seat). **On the bed**, five local seats, 420 s, the
   harness's new `-NoVoteNodes` (a client that plays every turn and says no `TIMEOUT_VOTE` and no
   `TIMEOUT_CERT`), each plan first on the rules before (`S1-HY` fixed first: the knob had reached every node):
     - **a turn**, n2 silent from its first action after 60 s, n3 never voting. Before (`run095849-5`): the
       turn stood from the four clocks running out at 96-100 s to the run's end, the tally at 3/4 -- two hands
       in 420 s. After (`run102155-5`): the tally stood at 3/4 from 105.6 s; at 138.7 s the three voted about
       n3 as a silent voter, the certificate completed at 139.6 s -- *certified seat 2's timeout, unanimously
       among [0, 1, 4], and takes the veto of seat 3* -- and the table acted for seat 2 at 139.7 s; the hand's
       later stage that needed seat 2 was certified among the three alone in under a second, the roster went to
       `[0, 1, 3, 4]`, and 36 hands finished, one genesis on all five.
     - **a dead seat**, n2 killed at 120 s for good, n3 never voting. Before (`run100551-5`): the hand waiting
       on seat 2 stood at 3/4 from 160 s and ended on its deadline at 191 s naming nobody, the next opened with
       the same five -- and it recovered only because the non-voting client had sealed the certificate about
       seat 2 alone, from its own unsent vote and the three it heard, and opened the next hand at a genesis of
       its own: that hand waited on seats 2 and 3, D-036 certified both at 222.6 s, and seat 3 spent a return
       to come back at hand #16. After (`run102859-5`): the tally stood at 3/4 from 160.6 s, the silent vote came
       at 190.6 s, one certificate named seat 2 and seat 3, the roster went to `[0, 1, 3, 4]` at 191.7 s with
       seat 3 kept -- no fork, no return -- and 33 hands finished, one genesis on all five.
     - **two regressions** on the same build: no knob at all (`run103601-5`): 42 hands on all five, one
       genesis, not one vote; n2 silent at its turn with everybody voting (`run104304-5`): the ordinary
       certificate at 4/4 in under a second of the clocks, *the table acted for seat 2: Fold* at 99.1 s, 38
       hands, one genesis, and no silent vote anywhere -- D-065 speaks only where a vote does not come.

**Amended the same day (the owner: *continue with what remains*) -- the question comes early.** Asked at the
stage's deadline, the question came when the table was itself about to vote the asker out: a seat that cannot hear
one member lost a whole budget at every event of that member's, and the others, needing its next event, voted about
it on the same clock -- and `D-059` cuts their patience after the first wait. So a voter asks five seconds into the
stage (`QUESTION_AFTER_MS`) when it holds an event of a later stage of the hand signed by a seat other than the
subject and itself (`Hand::later_frame_from_another`): that seat moved past the stage, which no seat does without
the subject's event, so it will never vote about the subject there and the early vote can complete no certificate.
Measured with two new harness knobs: `-DeafToNode/-DeafToSeat/-DeafToAt/-DeafToFor` (one client hears nothing the
named seat's member delivers itself; copies other members send still arrive) and `-NoAnswerNodes`
(`P2P_POKER_NO_ANSWER`: a client answers no vote). Five seats, n1 deaf to seat 3 from 90 s for 90 s. *Without the
answer* (`run132920-5`, every node): n1 voted about seat 3 twice and nobody re-sent the frame; n1 stalled in hand
#8, the four others certified seat 1 out of that hand at 149.5 s and out of the next at 171.5 s and took it off the
table (172.4 s); its hearing back, n1 found the table at hand #10, took it up as a bystander from four copies
(`D-038`) and was certified back in at 195.6 s, five seats again at 198.7 s -- seat 1 finished 31 hands of the
table's 33. *With it* (`run131008-5`): n1 asked eleven times, six seconds apart whenever it lacked seat 3's event,
and each time seat 0 -- the lowest seat neither named nor asking -- sent the frame again (seat 3 re-sent its own
too, which the knob kept from n1); no certificate was made, every seat finished all 33 hands, one genesis. Times
on n0's clock.


## D-066 — half the table silent: the half with the lowest seat goes on, and any two after five minutes

**Decided 2026-09-18 by the project owner** -- the choice *"Tie-break + 5 min"*, offered with its price: a real
partition of the network that outlasts five minutes splits the table into two games -- under the owner's requirement
of the same day that no phase may stand.

1. **The case.** D-036's floor lets no group short of a majority certify the rest, and D-065 counts the silent voters
   among the named. Where the seats that stopped were half the live seats or more -- two of four behind one line,
   typically -- nothing could remove them: every cryptographic stage ended on its deadline naming nobody and the next
   hand opened with the same seats, a turn stood until `hand_deadline_ms` (29 min at a four-seat Sit & Go), and the
   window could only ask the player to wait or to leave (`S1-DI`).
2. **Exactly half: the half holding the lowest seat.** A certificate with `|V(S)| = |Q|` -- `Q` the seats named that
   did not resign -- and two voters at least is legal when the lowest seat of `V(S) ∪ Q` is in `V(S)`. One half of a
   table holds that seat and the other never does, so the two halves of a partition never certify each other
   (`Hand::floor_holds_for`).
3. **Five minutes gone: any two.** A seat the stage waits on that has been out of the table's group, or silent there,
   for `LONG_GONE_S` = 300 s by a voter's own reading -- counted only while the voter's own line is sound
   (`note_unheard`, `own_line_suspect`) -- is voted about at once with `cause = 3` (`CAUSE_LONG_GONE`), and a voter
   that already voted about it at that stage without the cause votes again with it: a turn standing to the hand's
   budget has no next stage to carry it. A certificate whose every waited-on seat carries the cause needs two voters
   and no majority. The seats it names leave the roster as quiet seats do, and come back by D-028's return.
4. **Never over a seat that is here.** Neither exception is taken by a seat it names as waited-on: that client knows
   it is here, which is the one fact such a certificate may not overrule. A half or a minority that lied about the
   rest therefore forks away alone -- the honest seats never bank it and go on among themselves -- and a seat really
   gone never hears it. The voters take their own certificate, so a present seat that stalls at exactly half cannot
   hold its accusers.
5. **The price**, accepted by the owner: a real partition that outlasts `LONG_GONE_S` splits the table, each half
   certifying the other and playing on. Before this the table waited for ever.
6. **Measured.**
   In the engine: `half_the_table_holding_the_lowest_seat_certifies_the_other_half`, `the_half_without_the_lowest_seat_waits`,
   `a_certificate_half_the_table_carries_is_not_taken_by_a_seat_it_names`, `seats_long_gone_are_certified_by_two_short_of_a_majority`
   (and a seat named that is here keeps its table), `tests/timeout_certificate.rs`
   `half_the_table_gone_at_a_turn_goes_on_after_five_minutes` (four seats played to a turn, the seat to act and seat 0
   gone together: the turn stands, and after the five minutes the two vote again with the cause, name the other as a
   silent voter, and the table acts for the seat); the window's `floor_at_table` answers the tie-break as the engine
   does (`half_the_table_holding_the_lowest_seat_is_no_question`). **On the bed**, four local seats, two killed together
   at 120 s, each plan first on the D-065 build:
     - **the half left holds seat 0** (n2 and n3 killed). Before (`run113002-4`): the kills fell on a turn of seat 2's,
       the tally stood at 2/3 from 158 s -- seat 3, gone, a voter -- the window said the two could not certify the two,
       and the turn stood to the run's end, nine hands in 420 s. After (`run113706-4`): hand #12 waited at its opening on
       seats 2 and 3, the clocks ran out at 158.5 s, *the table has certified seats [2, 3]'s timeout, unanimously among
       [0, 1]* at 159.8 s, the roster went to `[0, 1]` at 160.6 s and heads-up play went on: 51 hands, one genesis.
     - **the half left does not hold it** (n0 and n1 killed, the founder among them). Before (`run114410-4`): a turn of
       seat 0's stood at 2/3 from 156 s to the run's end at 540 s. After (`run115311-4`): the same turn stood at 2/3 -- the
       tie-break does not let the half without seat 0 go on -- until *seat 0 has been out of the table's group for 5 min*
       at 539 s, when the two voted again with the cause and the table went on: 20 hands on both, one genesis. The five
       minutes came 100 s late: two seats timing out of the library's group together tripped `own_line_suspect`'s *two
       timeouts in a minute*, which cleared the count; the gate is now *this client hears no other seat of the table*.
       Again on that build (`run121458-4`): the kills fell on a hand's opening, so every hand ended on its deadline
       with the four seats -- one every 32 s, the window saying *once they have been gone 5 min they can (D-066)* --
       until 442.9 s, five minutes after the silence was read, when *the table has certified seats [0, 1]'s timeout,
       unanimously among [2, 3]* (446.5 s) and heads-up play went on: 45 hands opened on both, one genesis.
     - **a regression**, no knob (`run120313-4`): 46 hands, one genesis, not one vote.

**Amended the same day -- the line, and the seat that was gone.** Two things the bed and a closer reading taught.
(1) *Whose line is sound.* The count of five minutes runs only while this client hears some other seat of the
table **and** its library is on the network: two players at one end of a table who lose their line together still
hear each other over their own LAN, and would otherwise count the far end gone and split the table. (2) *A seat that
was gone takes its certificate.* The refusal of point 4 held for a seat whose own line was up all the while; a seat
whose line was down within `LONG_GONE_S` (the node's `line_down_at`) takes a certificate half the table carries
about it -- it may really have been gone -- and comes back by D-028's return. Each hand is told as it opens, before
the copies it holds replay (`line_down_within`): a hand taken up after an outage may carry the very certificate
that named the seat while it was away, and the first build read the line only at the next stall tick -- a review
of the change caught it before a run did. The window's note, the table's word
about a seat out for good (`D-047`) and the engine now read one floor. Measured, `run131711-4` (times on n0's
clock): four seats, n2 and n3 lost their internet together at 120 s for 150 s; the half left -- seat 0 in it --
acted for seat 2 at its turn at 158.4 s, naming seat 3 a silent voter, certified seat 3 in the next hand (202.5 s)
and played heads-up from 203.5 s; n2 and n3, their lines back, found the table far on, took up its running hand
#26 as bystanders from the others' copies (`D-038`), asked to sit in, and were certified back in by the two at
286.6 s -- the table was four again from hand #27 at 290.2 s, 48 hands, one genesis on all four.

## D-067 — the lobby is a card room, not a network console

**Decided 2026-09-18 by the project owner**, who asked for a lobby that the poker community would take to on
sight -- attractive, plain to a newcomer within five seconds, a table found by a regular within two -- in the
table window's own style (`D-048`), with everything technical kept but moved out of the first view.

1. **The case.** The lobby's first line read *0 tables, 0 open, 132 peers, 0 in lobby, 0 searching*; the largest
   text below it was a client log of DHT walks; the strip said *27 dials failed*; and the one thing a player wanted
   -- a game -- was a green button among three at the bottom of a list of eight columns. Four zeroes read as an
   empty restaurant, a DHT count reads as players when it is not, and a log of peer ids is a thing an operator
   reads. At 200 % text the three columns drew over each other and the buttons over the list.
2. **What it says now.** A band of the table's felt with its gold keyline, the mark, the name and the claim the
   room is built on -- *No house. No server. Every card proven.* -- with the four sentences behind it one click
   away, its fourth being what the cryptography does not stop (`gui::lobby::FAIR_PLAY`). Under it the one large
   gold button, *FIND A GAME*, which starts the search on the click with the format chosen beside it; *Create
   table* beside it, quieter; an honest line on what to expect. The tables are cards: the name, the game as a
   badge whose hover says what the game is, the seats **drawn** -- a gold disc per player, a ring per empty seat,
   filling over a third of a second as a seat is taken -- and what the table is doing in a sentence a player acts
   on (*waiting for 2 more*, *1 seat left*, *full*, *rules changed*). The selected card carries its own *Join*; a
   double click sits down. An empty list is an invitation with the suits over it. The player has a card of their
   own: the table's avatar, the name, how long they have been here, and their record. The connection is one light
   and one word -- *Online*, *Online through a relay*, *Connecting…*, and red only for the one real fault, an
   unreachable client with no relay -- with *Network details* beside it, which opens what the strip used to say and
   the client log under it.
3. **The rules the words follow**, each a function with a test in `gui::lobby`: nothing is ever invented -- not a
   player, not a number, not a wait (`headline_counts` says only what is there and never a zero; `hero_note` names
   no number before one was measured; the DHT's peers are in the details and are not players); a result is stated
   and a win congratulated, and nothing asks for the chips back (`result_words`, `result_praise`); the session's
   length is said and never nagged about (`session_words`); no fabricated scarcity, no streak, no daily reward. The
   lobby's gold **is** the table's, measured: `theme::GOLD_ACTION` is `style::COLOR_ACCENT` and `GOLD_EDGE` is
   `BOX_ACCENT`, asserted, and used for the one action, a win and a selected table's edge only.
4. **The record.** `storage::results` (`results.cbor` in the profile, at most 500 entries) keeps the place this
   player finished each Sit & Go in, written by the window from the node's `Finished` word at the boundary and
   from nothing else (`S1-FL`); a cash game has no place and leaves no entry. Local and private, as the notes are.
5. **The width decides the columns** (`render::columns_for`): three from 980 points, two from 660, one below --
   the tables, with the people and the card behind a *People* button. A 1 180-pixel window at 200 % is 590 points.
   A column too short for the way in and the list both (under 420 points) scrolls as one. Photographed at 100 % and
   200 % text in 1 180×760 and 900×600 windows, with a headless founder on the LAN for a row to draw: nothing runs
   past an edge, every function reachable.
6. **Unchanged, and checked by hand on the build**: the search (`D-064`, its modal and *More options…*), creating
   and sitting down (the dialogs), the lobby chat and who is here, the unfinished game, the relay notice
   (`D-002`), the four-tab settings, `D-043`'s *Your tables*, and every rule the pane carried before -- a table
